# ci-cd

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://docs.github.com/en/actions/get-started/continuous-integration ; https://dora.dev/capabilities/continuous-delivery/
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: the pipeline is configured from this repo's own build/test commands and branch layout, read directly; no other skill's output is an input. Feeds deployment-strategies, preview-environments, rollback.
- **Feeds into:** deployment-strategies, preview-environments, rollback

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Setting up or auditing the automated pipeline that builds, tests, publishes, and deploys a project — workflow files, branch protection, artifact publishing, deploy jobs, and delivery metrics.
- **Do NOT use when:** Choosing how a release rolls out to users (rolling, blue-green, canary) — that is deployment-strategies. Building the images the pipeline publishes — that is containers.

## Rules

1. **DO-001 — One pipeline definition, in the repo.** The whole pipeline lives in version-controlled workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml` or the platform equivalent); no build or deploy step exists only in a console, a wiki, or someone's shell history.
2. **DO-002 — Fixed stage order.** Every run executes in order: checkout → install → lint → build → unit tests → integration tests → end-to-end tests → publish artifact → deploy jobs per environment. A stage may be empty only when the project genuinely has none of that test type, recorded in progress.md.
3. **DO-003 — The pipeline triggers on push and pull request, and its checks are required.** The build/test workflow runs on every push and every pull request, and its status checks are required checks on the protected branch, so a failing run blocks merge.
4. **DO-004 — Prove the pipeline can fail.** Before the gate is trusted, open a throwaway pull request containing a deliberately failing test and confirm the check reports failure and merge is blocked; record the drill result in progress.md. Repeat after any workflow or branch-protection change.
5. **DO-005 — Build once, promote the same artifact.** The artifact deployed to production is bit-identical to the one tested in staging; deploy jobs reference it by digest or immutable version tag, never by rebuilding from source.
6. **DO-006 — Gating jobs run everything, for real.** No skipped tests, no `continue-on-error`, and no commented-out steps on any job whose check is required; a step that cannot run is fixed or the job stops being a gate and the change is recorded.
7. **DO-007 — Install from the lockfile, in CI only.** Dependencies install with the lockfile-frozen command (`npm ci`, `--frozen-lockfile`, or the ecosystem equivalent); nothing installs dependencies at container start or deploy time.
8. **DO-008 — Every deploy leaves a record.** Each deploy writes one record containing the artifact digest, the commit SHA, who or what triggered it, and the timestamp; the live revision of every environment is identifiable from these records alone.
9. **DO-009 — Dependency updates flow as automated pull requests.** Dependabot or Renovate is configured for the project's ecosystems and base images, and CI scans dependencies and images for known vulnerabilities, failing the run on critical findings.
10. **DO-010 — Workflow files are linted in CI.** The pipeline runs a workflow linter (e.g., actionlint) on its own workflow files; a lint error fails the run like any other check.
11. **DO-011 — Secrets come from the CI secret store only.** Workflow files reference secrets by name from the platform secret store; no credential value is written into a workflow file, echoed into logs, or passed to builds triggered by untrusted forks.
12. **DO-012 — Delivery is measured with the DORA four keys.** Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change fail rate, and failed-deployment recovery time are computed from pipeline and incident records on a regular cadence and reviewed in progress.md — never estimated from memory.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-001 — Decorative CI.** Banned: a workflow exists but its checks are not required, so merges proceed on red. Defeats: DET-INF-002. Bad: the test workflow runs only on pushes to `main`, after the merge it was meant to gate. Instead: make the build/test checks required status checks on the protected branch so a failure blocks merge. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-002 — Neutered gating job.** Banned: skipped tests, `continue-on-error`, or commented-out steps on a job whose check is required. Defeats: DET-INF-002. Bad: the test job carries `continue-on-error: true` "until the flaky tests are fixed." Instead: remove the silencer, fix or quarantine the failing test in the open, and let a red job fail the run. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-003 — Hand-carried deploy.** Banned: deploying by copying files over FTP/SFTP, SSHing in to `git pull` and restart, or building on the production server. Defeats: DET-INF-004. Bad: the release step rsyncs the working tree to the server and restarts the process by hand. Instead: the pipeline's deploy job promotes the CI-built immutable artifact and writes a deploy record. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-004 — Floating production artifact.** Banned: production deploys reference a `latest` tag, an ungated branch HEAD, or whatever installs at container start. Defeats: DET-INF-026. Bad: the deploy job runs `docker pull app:latest`, so every restart is an untested upgrade. Instead: deploy the exact digest recorded when the artifact was published and tested. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-005 — Dependency time capsule.** Banned: no automated update tool configured and no vulnerability scan in CI, so the lockfile and base images age untouched from creation day. Defeats: DET-INF-025. Bad: six months after setup there is no Dependabot/Renovate config and no scan step; the base image tag predates two security releases. Instead: enable automated update pull requests and add a CI scan step that fails on critical findings. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-DO-001 — Broken-test drill (automated).** Verifies: DO-003, DO-004. Check: open a throwaway pull request with a deliberately failing test; query the check-run status via the platform API and confirm the required check concludes `failure` and the branch ruleset reports merge blocked. Before a production environment is provisioned, this gate's disposition is a recorded provisioning waiver per §6.3; it unblocks when a hosted platform with branch rulesets and a check-runs API exists and the drill has been run there. Pass: check is red and merge is refused. Fail: block shipment — the gate is decoration until the drill passes. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-002 — Artifact identity check (automated).** Verifies: DO-005, DO-008. Check: script reads the artifact digest from the staging deploy record and the production deploy record for the same release and compares them (`test "$STAGING_DIGEST" = "$PROD_DIGEST"`). Pass: digests are identical. Fail: block shipment and rebuild the promotion path. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-003 — Workflow lint (automated).** Verifies: DO-001, DO-010. Check: run `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml` (or the platform's equivalent linter) as a CI step. Pass: exit code 0. Fail: block merge until the workflow files lint clean. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-004 — Gating-job integrity scan (automated).** Verifies: DO-006. Check: `grep -rn "continue-on-error: *true\|skipTests\|test.skip" .github/workflows/` returns no hits inside jobs wired to required checks. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block merge; remove the silencer or un-require the check with the change recorded. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-005 — Deploy-record audit (manual).** Verifies: DO-008, DO-012. Check: open the deploy records for the last three production deploys; each must resolve to an artifact digest, a commit SHA, a triggering actor, and a timestamp, and the DORA figures in progress.md must be recomputable from these records plus the incident log. Pass: all three records complete and the metrics recompute. Fail: warn, and fix the record-keeping before the next release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Pipeline as documentation.** Beautiful workflow YAML that has not run in weeks because triggers were narrowed to manual dispatch; catch it by checking the date of the last run, not the file.
- **Snowflake staging.** Staging was hand-tweaked (extra env values, a manual hotfix) until a green staging run no longer predicts production; catch it by diffing staging's effective config against what the pipeline would produce.
- **Slow-feedback batching.** The pipeline takes so long that everyone batches huge pull requests to suffer it once; the gate still passes, but review quality and lead time quietly rot. Watch pull request size alongside pipeline duration.
- **Metrics theater.** DORA numbers quoted in a review that nobody can recompute from pipeline and incident records; if the figures have no query or export behind them, they are decoration.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — A gate that actually gates](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects DO-003, DO-006.
- [Example 2 — Build once, promote the digest](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects DO-005.
- [Example 3 — Lockfile install, CI only](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects DO-007.

## Recall anchors

- If a red pipeline can still merge, there is no pipeline.
- Build once; promote the digest, never rebuild for production.
- A gate you have not deliberately broken is a gate you are assuming.
- Every deploy leaves a record: digest, SHA, actor, time.
- DORA numbers come from records, not from vibes.

## Checklist

- [ ] Pipeline definition is committed and triggers on push and pull request (DO-001, DO-002).
- [ ] Build/test checks are required on the protected branch (DO-003).
- [ ] Broken-test drill performed and recorded after the last workflow or protection change (DO-004).
- [ ] Staging and production deploy records show the identical artifact digest (DO-005).
- [ ] No `continue-on-error`, skipped tests, or commented-out steps on gating jobs (DO-006).
- [ ] Dependencies install from the lockfile in CI; nothing installs at container start or deploy time (DO-007).
- [ ] Last three deploys each resolve to digest, commit SHA, actor, and timestamp (DO-008).
- [ ] Automated dependency-update pull requests are flowing and the CI vulnerability scan is green (DO-009).

<!-- generated from skills/devops-deployment/cloud-costs/SKILL.md -->

# cloud-costs

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://learn.microsoft.com/cloud-computing/finops/framework/finops-framework ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/getting-started-ad.html
- **Depends on:** free-tiers, infrastructure-as-code, scaling
- **Feeds into:** reliability, hosting

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** the project spends anything on cloud resources, or is about to; when a bill, budget, or cost estimate is produced; when autoscaling, instance sizing, or commitment discounts are decided; when "optimisation" work is proposed.
- **Do NOT use when:** the stack runs entirely on free tiers and nothing is billed — free-tiers governs that posture, and this skill takes over the moment the first paid line item appears. Do not use this skill to choose providers; hosting does that.

## Rules

1. **DO-321 — Allocate at least 90% of spend.** Billing data is allocated to a named service and team via tags or separate accounts, following the FinOps Inform phase, until at least 90% of monthly spend carries an owner. Unallocated spend above 10% is recorded as a finding in the monthly review, not absorbed as overhead.
2. **DO-322 — Budget before workloads.** Every cloud account or billing project has a budget with alerts at multiple thresholds (actual and forecasted spend) before its first workload is created. An account with resources and no budget fails G-DO-162.
3. **DO-323 — Anomaly detection from day one.** Provider anomaly detection (for example AWS Cost Anomaly Detection) is enabled on every billing account when the account is created, because a misconfigured autoscaler or a runaway job bills hourly, long before a monthly review would notice.
4. **DO-324 — Tags are enforced at creation.** Mandatory allocation tags (service, team, environment) are applied by IaC defaults or provider tag policies at resource creation. Backfilling tags before an audit is not enforcement; a resource created in the console without tags fails G-DO-163.
5. **DO-325 — Report unit costs next to revenue.** Each month, compute at least one unit cost — cost per request, per active user, or per paying customer — from the allocated billing data and record it next to the matching revenue or usage figure. A total bill with no unit cost cannot show whether growth is efficient or just bigger.
6. **DO-326 — Every autoscaling ceiling is a recorded cost decision.** No autoscaler runs without a maximum (replicas, instances, concurrency). The maximum, the monthly cost at that maximum, and who approved it are recorded where the scaling configuration lives (see scaling); an unbounded autoscaler fails review under BAN-DO-161.
7. **DO-327 — Sweep waste on a cadence.** At least monthly, list idle instances, oversized databases, orphaned disks/snapshots/storage, and resources with no owner tag; each item is deleted, resized, or ticketed with a named owner and a decision date. A waste item carried for two consecutive sweeps with no decision is escalated in the monthly review.
8. **DO-328 — Rightsize from observed utilization, at least quarterly.** Instance and database sizes are reviewed at least once a quarter against observed p95 CPU/memory utilization over the trailing 30 days. Sizes set at launch and never revisited are presumed wrong in one direction or the other.
9. **DO-329 — Commitments only against a measured baseline.** Reserved capacity, savings plans, or committed-use discounts are bought only for the steady-state baseline proven by at least 30 days of allocated usage data. Committing to unmeasured workloads converts a discount into a fixed liability.
10. **DO-330 — Optimisation never removes protection.** Cost work never disables or degrades backups, monitoring, alerting, or redundancy. Those are the product's safety properties, not overhead; a savings proposal that touches them is rejected under BAN-DO-163 and the saving is found elsewhere.
11. **DO-331 — The first paid line item needs its recorded trigger.** While a project is in the $0 free-tier posture, no paid resource is created until the trigger named in the free-tier sheet fires (first real user, first payment, cap forecast) and the spend is recorded. A paid resource whose first notice is the invoice fails this rule.
12. **DO-332 — File a monthly cost review.** Each month produces a short review artifact: allocation percentage, budget and anomaly alert status, unit cost, waste actions taken and open, and the date of the last rightsizing review. The review is the Operate phase made visible; no artifact means the month's spend was unreviewed.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-161 — Unbounded autoscaling.** Banned: an autoscaler, function concurrency setting, or replica range with no maximum. Defeats: DET-INF-027. Bad: an HPA with `maxReplicas` unset scales to 60 pods overnight on a traffic spike from a stuck retry loop, and the first notice is the monthly invoice. Instead: set a maximum sized from the load-test ceiling in scaling, record the monthly cost at that maximum and its approver per DO-326. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-162 — Untagged console-created resources.** Banned: creating billable resources by hand in the provider console, outside IaC and without allocation tags. Defeats: DET-INF-024. Bad: a developer launches a large instance from the console for a "quick test"; it runs a side project for a year, appears in no stack, and its cost belongs to nobody. Instead: create resources through IaC with mandatory tags applied by default per DO-324, and terminate the resource the day the test ends. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-163 — "Savings" by removing protection.** Banned: presenting disabled backups, monitoring, alerting, or redundancy as a cost optimisation. Defeats: DET-INF-008. Bad: a cost review "saves" money by turning off database backups and deleting the second replica; the saving is real until the first incident, which is now unrecoverable. Instead: find the saving in waste — idle, oversized, or orphaned resources per DO-327 — and leave protection intact per DO-330. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-164 — Budget alert routed to nobody.** Banned: a budget or anomaly alert whose notifications go to an unmonitored inbox, a departed team member, or no destination at all. Defeats: DET-INF-012. Bad: the 80% budget alert fires into a shared mailbox nobody reads; the overrun is discovered from the invoice three weeks later. Instead: route budget and anomaly alerts to a channel a named on-call or owner reads, and prove delivery with a test notification at setup per DO-322 and DO-323. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-DO-161 — Allocation coverage (automated).** Verifies: DO-321, DO-324. Check: from the provider billing export (for example `aws ce get-cost-and-usage` grouped by the service tag over the last full month), compute tagged spend ÷ total spend. Pass: allocation ≥90%. Fail: block the monthly review sign-off; untagged sources are named as findings. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-162 — Budget and anomaly coverage (automated).** Verifies: DO-322, DO-323. Check: `aws budgets describe-budgets` (or the provider equivalent) lists at least one budget with actual and forecasted alert thresholds for every account, and `aws ce get-anomaly-monitors` returns an active monitor. Pass: every account has both. Fail: block creation of new workloads in any uncovered account. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-163 — Tag coverage at creation.** Verifies: DO-324. Check: sample the resources created since the last review from the billing export or resource inventory; count those missing any mandatory tag (service, team, environment). Pass: zero untagged billable resources. Fail: tag or terminate each offender and record how it bypassed IaC defaults. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-164 — Monthly review freshness.** Verifies: DO-325, DO-327, DO-328, DO-332. Check: open the cost review artifact for the current month and confirm it records the allocation percentage, a unit cost, waste actions with owners, and a rightsizing review dated within the last quarter. Pass: all four present and current. Fail: the month's spend is marked unreviewed and the review is completed before the next billing cycle closes. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Invoice-driven management.** Costs are only ever looked at when the invoice arrives, so every surprise is a month old before anyone can act. Catch it by asking for this month's forecasted spend — if the answer needs the invoice, DO-322 and DO-323 were skipped.
- **Dashboard theatre.** A cost dashboard exists and looks impressive, but no review artifact, no waste tickets, and no decisions ever come out of it. Catch it by asking what changed because of the dashboard last month; visibility without the Operate loop is decoration.
- **Optimising the visible line.** Shaving the biggest line item (usually compute) while a quieter one — data transfer, storage growth, per-seat tooling — compounds unchecked. Catch it by reviewing the top five line items' month-over-month deltas, not just the largest absolute number.
- **Launch-size forever.** Production still runs the instance sizes guessed on day one, months after real utilization data exists. Catch it by comparing each major resource's size against its trailing-30-day p95 utilization; a mismatch with no ticket means DO-328 lapsed.
- **Preview sprawl billed as production.** Forgotten preview and staging environments run around the clock at production sizes. Catch it in the waste sweep: non-production environments carry schedules or smaller sizes, and anything unowned is terminated per DO-327.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Autoscaler with no ceiling](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects DO-326.
- [Example 2 — Console instance nobody owns](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects DO-324.
- [Example 3 — "Optimisation" that deletes the backups](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects DO-330.

## Recall anchors

- Unallocated spend is a finding, not a rounding error.
- Budget alert before workloads, never after the invoice.
- Every autoscaling ceiling is a cost decision with a name on it.
- Never save money by switching off backups or monitoring.
- $0 until the recorded trigger fires; commitments only on measured baselines.

## Checklist

- [ ] At least 90% of last month's spend is allocated to a named service and team. (DO-321)
- [ ] Every account has a budget with actual and forecasted alerts, created before its workloads. (DO-322)
- [ ] Anomaly detection is active on every billing account and its alerts reach a named reader. (DO-323, BAN-DO-164)
- [ ] No autoscaler runs without a recorded maximum and approved cost at that maximum. (DO-326)
- [ ] The monthly waste sweep ran; every idle, oversized, or orphaned resource is deleted, resized, or ticketed with an owner and date. (DO-327)
- [ ] Rightsizing was reviewed within the last quarter against observed p95 utilization. (DO-328)
- [ ] No savings proposal touches backups, monitoring, alerting, or redundancy. (DO-330)
- [ ] The monthly cost review artifact is filed with allocation %, unit cost, and open waste actions. (DO-332)

<!-- generated from skills/devops-deployment/containers/SKILL.md -->

# containers

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Docker Docs, "Building best practices" — https://docs.docker.com/build/building/best-practices/ ; DORA, "Continuous delivery" capability (build once, promote the same artifact) — https://dora.dev/capabilities/continuous-delivery/
- **Depends on:** ci-cd
- **Feeds into:** deployment-strategies, kubernetes, servers-vps, hosting, rollback

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a service is packaged for deployment — writing or reviewing its Dockerfile, image tagging, build pipeline, or the image reference a deploy actually runs.
- **Do NOT use when:** the workload runs on a platform that builds and runs the artifact itself with no Dockerfile in the repo (use hosting instead), or for orchestrator manifests and scaling policy (use kubernetes / scaling).

## Rules

1. **DO-061 — One Dockerfile per service, multi-stage.** Each service has exactly one Dockerfile at its root: a build stage with the full toolchain, and a final runtime stage carrying only the built artifact and its runtime dependencies — no compiler, SDK, or build cache in the final stage.
2. **DO-062 — Pin every base image.** Base images are pinned to a specific version tag (e.g. `node:22.11-alpine`); production builds pin by digest (`node:22.11-alpine@sha256:…`). An unpinned or major-only tag (`node`, `node:22`) fails review.
3. **DO-063 — No secrets in any layer.** No secret value appears in `ENV`, `ARG`, `COPY`, or any intermediate layer. Build-time secrets use BuildKit secret mounts (`--mount=type=secret`); runtime secrets are injected by the platform at start.
4. **DO-064 — Final stage runs non-root.** The final stage creates a dedicated user and sets `USER` to it before `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT`. A final stage with no `USER` instruction runs as root and fails review.
5. **DO-065 — Dependencies before source.** The Dockerfile copies the dependency manifest and lockfile and installs dependencies before copying application source, so source-only changes reuse the dependency layer. Installs run in CI mode from the lockfile (`npm ci`, `--frozen-lockfile`, or the ecosystem equivalent).
6. **DO-066 — Committed `.dockerignore`.** Every build context has a committed `.dockerignore` excluding at minimum `.git`, `.env*`, `node_modules` (or the local dependency dir), and local build output, so secrets and local artifacts never enter the context.
7. **DO-067 — One process per container, exec form.** Each container runs exactly one foreground process, started with exec-form `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` (JSON array), so the application is PID 1 and receives `SIGTERM` directly. Supporting processes (database, cache, cron) are separate containers.
8. **DO-068 — Immutable tags, never `latest`.** Images are tagged with the release version and commit SHA and referenced by version tag or digest in every deploy spec. The exact image reference of each deploy is recorded with the deploy.
9. **DO-069 — Scanned in CI, rebuilt on a schedule.** Every image is vulnerability-scanned in CI before promotion, and base images are rebuilt on a regular cadence (at least monthly, and on critical base-image advisories) so patches actually land instead of aging in a pinned tag.
10. **DO-070 — Health is declared.** The image declares a `HEALTHCHECK`, or the deploy platform's probe is configured against the app's health endpoint, so a hung process is detected and restarted rather than judged by the homepage loading.
11. **DO-071 — Resource limits are set.** Every deployed container declares CPU and memory limits (compose `deploy.resources`, platform settings, or orchestrator spec) sized from observed usage; an unbounded container that can starve its neighbours fails review.
12. **DO-072 — Logs go to stdout/stderr only.** The application writes logs to stdout/stderr and never to files inside the container, so logs survive via the platform's log pipeline instead of vanishing with the container filesystem.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-031 — Floating `latest` tag in a deploy spec.** Banned: production or staging deploys referencing `image: app:latest` (or no tag). Defeats: DET-INF-026. Bad: compose file ships `image: myapp:latest`, so every restart silently pulls different code. Instead: reference the immutable artifact built in CI, e.g. `image: myapp:1.4.2@sha256:9f2c…`, and record that reference with the deploy. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-032 — Secret baked into the image.** Banned: a real credential in `ENV`/`ARG`, or `COPY .env` into any stage. Defeats: DET-INF-005. Bad: `ENV DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:realpassword@db/app` in the Dockerfile. Instead: pass the value at runtime from the platform's secret store, and use `--mount=type=secret` for anything needed during the build. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-033 — Installing dependencies at container start.** Banned: `npm install`, `pip install`, or equivalent in the entrypoint or start command. Defeats: DET-INF-026. Bad: `CMD ["sh", "-c", "npm install && node server.js"]` — every restart is an untested upgrade. Instead: install from the lockfile in the build stage (`npm ci`) so the shipped image already contains its dependencies. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-034 — Root by default in the final stage.** Banned: a final stage with no `USER` instruction, leaving the base image's root default in production. Defeats: DET-INF-022. Bad: the Dockerfile ends at `COPY --from=build /app /app` and the process runs as uid 0. Instead: create an unprivileged user in the final stage (`RUN adduser -D app`) and set `USER app` before the entrypoint. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-035 — Frozen base image, never rebuilt or scanned.** Banned: pinning a base image once and shipping it indefinitely with no CI scan and no rebuild cadence. Defeats: DET-INF-025. Bad: `FROM node:18.0-alpine` untouched for a year, scan step absent from the pipeline. Instead: scan every image in CI and rebuild on the scheduled cadence, advancing the pin through reviewed update PRs. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-DO-031 — Dockerfile lint.** Verifies: DO-061, DO-064, DO-067. Check: `hadolint Dockerfile` runs in CI for every Dockerfile in the repo. Pass: exit code 0 with no errors. Fail: block merge until the Dockerfile is fixed. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-032 — Image vulnerability scan.** Verifies: DO-069. Check: `trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed <image-ref>` on the built image before promotion. Pass: exit code 0 — no fixable critical vulnerabilities. Fail: block promotion; patch or rebase the image. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-033 — Deploy reference is pinned.** Verifies: DO-062, DO-068. Check: scripted grep over deploy specs — `grep -rnE 'image:\s*\S+:(latest)?\s*$' docker-compose*.yml deploy/ k8s/` must return nothing, and the recorded deploy reference contains a version tag or `@sha256:` digest. Pass: no floating reference found; staging and production records show the identical digest. Fail: block the deploy. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-034 — No secret in the built image.** Verifies: DO-063, DO-066. Check: `docker inspect --format '{{json .Config.Env}}' <image-ref>` contains no credential values, and `docker history --no-trunc <image-ref>` shows no `ENV`/`ARG`/`COPY` step carrying a secret; `.dockerignore` exists in the build context. Pass: both inspections clean. Fail: block promotion and rotate any exposed credential. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-035 — Runtime smoke test.** Verifies: DO-064, DO-067, DO-070. Check: start the image; `docker exec <id> whoami` must not print `root`; `docker stop` must exit the container within the stop grace period (clean SIGTERM handling); the health check reports healthy. Pass: all three hold. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **The everything container.** App server, database, and a cron job run side by side in one container under a shell script. Catch it: more than one long-lived process in `docker top`; split into one container per process instead.
- **Rebuild-per-environment.** Staging and production each build their own image from the same commit, so the tested artifact is not the shipped one. Catch it: compare the image digests recorded per environment — they must be identical; promote, never rebuild.
- **Cache-busting copy order.** `COPY . .` lands before the dependency install, so a one-line source change rebuilds the world and CI crawls. Catch it: read the Dockerfile top to bottom; manifests and lockfile must be copied and installed first.
- **Debugging inside the image.** The final image quietly keeps a shell, package manager, and dev dependencies "just in case". Catch it: check the final stage's package list against the runtime's real needs; debug with an ephemeral debug container, not a fat production image.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Floating single-stage Dockerfile vs pinned multi-stage](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects DO-061, DO-062.
- [Example 2 — Secret in `ENV` vs runtime injection](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects DO-063.
- [Example 3 — Root, shell-form start with install-at-start vs non-root exec form](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects DO-064, DO-067.

## Recall anchors

- Build once, pin the digest, promote the same image everywhere.
- Secrets ride at runtime or in BuildKit mounts — never in a layer.
- Final stage: slim, non-root, one process, exec form.
- Dependencies before source; installs happen at build time, never at start.
- If it is not scanned and rebuilt on a cadence, the pin is a time capsule.

## Checklist

- [ ] One multi-stage Dockerfile per service; final stage holds no compiler or SDK (DO-061).
- [ ] Every base image pinned to a version tag; production pinned by digest (DO-062).
- [ ] No secret in any `ENV`, `ARG`, or copied file; build secrets use BuildKit mounts (DO-063).
- [ ] Final stage sets a non-root `USER` (DO-064).
- [ ] Dependencies installed from the lockfile before source is copied (DO-065).
- [ ] `.dockerignore` committed and excludes `.git`, `.env*`, and local artifacts (DO-066).
- [ ] Exec-form entrypoint, one process per container, health check declared (DO-067, DO-070).
- [ ] Deploy specs reference a version tag or digest — never `latest` — and the reference is recorded per deploy (DO-068).
- [ ] CI scan passes with no fixable criticals; resource limits set on every container (DO-069, DO-071).

<!-- generated from skills/devops-deployment/deployment-strategies/SKILL.md -->

# deployment-strategies

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** GitHub Docs, "Managing environments for deployment" — https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.11/actions/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-deployments/managing-environments-for-deployment ; DORA, "Continuous delivery" — https://dora.dev/capabilities/continuous-delivery/ ; Kubernetes Docs, "Deployment" (rollout and rollback) — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/
- **Depends on:** ci-cd
- **Feeds into:** rollback, hosting, reliability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** choosing or changing how a release reaches production — the promotion path, the traffic-shift pattern, the abort conditions — or when a project's deploy is still manual, per-environment, or impossible to reverse.
- **Do NOT use when:** the pipeline itself does not exist yet (ci-cd builds it first), or the question is recovery after a bad deploy has already shipped (rollback owns the response; this skill owns making it possible).

## Rules

1. **DO-041 — Strategy chosen per change, and recorded.** Every release names its strategy — rolling (the default), blue-green, or canary — with the risk reason, in the deploy record. "We always deploy the same way" without a per-change risk check is not a strategy.
2. **DO-042 — No manual deploy steps.** No FTP/SFTP file copies, no SSH `git pull` + restart, no builds on the production server. Deploys run from CI off the built artifact, end to end.
3. **DO-043 — Build once, promote unchanged.** One immutable artifact (image digest or version tag) is promoted preview → staging → production. What was tested in staging is bit-identical to what ships.
4. **DO-044 — Every deploy leaves a record.** Artifact digest, commit SHA, strategy used, who/what triggered it, and when. The live production revision is identifiable from the record at any moment.
5. **DO-045 — Production sits behind environment protection.** The production deploy job runs only from the protected branch and only after the environment's protection rules pass (required reviewers, deployment-branch restrictions, wait timer where configured). For a single operator, the reviewer gate becomes a deliberate pause plus the release checklist — the gate is never silently deleted.
6. **DO-046 — Abort condition named before promotion.** Every blue-green or canary release names, in advance, the metric and threshold that sends traffic back (for example: error rate above baseline +1 percentage point for 5 minutes). A strategy without a written abort condition does not start.
7. **DO-047 — Database changes expand and contract.** Schema changes ship so old and new code both run against the new shape during the promotion window: add first, migrate reads/writes, remove the old shape in a later release.
8. **DO-048 — Config comes from the environment, never the artifact.** All deploy-varying values (URLs, credentials, toggles) arrive via environment variables or a config service per target. The artifact itself is identical in every environment.
9. **DO-049 — Deploy and release are separate events.** Risky user-visible changes deploy dark behind a feature flag; the flag flip is the release. Rollback of a flagged change is the flag flip first — seconds, no redeploy.
10. **DO-050 — Smoke-test the idle side before switching.** In blue-green, the idle environment passes its health check and a key-route smoke test before the router moves any traffic to it.
11. **DO-051 — Previous version stays returnable.** The old environment/artifact remains deployable until the new version clears its observation window. Tearing down the return path in the same action that ships is a failed deploy design.
12. **DO-052 — Canary promotion is metrics-gated, not clock-gated.** Each canary step compares error rate and latency against the pre-release baseline; traffic increases only while both stay within the DO-046 thresholds, and any breach aborts automatically or by the named operator action.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-021 — The hand-carried deploy.** Banned: shipping production changes by FTP/SFTP upload, SSH `git pull` + restart, or editing files on the live server. Defeats: DET-INF-004. Bad: the release note says "uploaded the new build folder and restarted the service" — nobody can say which commit is live. Instead: deploy from CI off the versioned artifact and record the digest and SHA (DO-042, DO-044). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-022 — The per-environment rebuild.** Banned: rebuilding the artifact for each environment, or deploying a floating target (`latest` tag, branch HEAD) instead of the tested artifact. Defeats: DET-INF-026. Bad: staging passed on Monday's build; production was rebuilt Wednesday "from the same code" with a newer transitive dependency. Instead: promote the one digest that passed staging, unchanged (DO-043). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-023 — Config baked into the artifact.** Banned: environment-specific URLs, hosts, or toggles compiled or copied into the artifact or a hand-edited per-server config file. Defeats: DET-INF-007. Bad: the production image contains `API_URL=https://api.example.com` as a source constant, so staging needs a different image. Instead: inject the value per target from environment variables or a config service (DO-048). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-024 — The abort-free rollout.** Banned: a canary or blue-green release with no pre-named metric, threshold, and return action. Defeats: DET-INF-017. Bad: "we'll watch the dashboard for a bit and roll back if it looks bad" — at 3 a.m. nobody knows what "bad" is or which button returns traffic. Instead: write the abort metric, threshold, and switch-back action into the release plan before promotion starts (DO-046). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-025 — The same-release contract.** Banned: dropping or renaming a database column/table in the same release that stops using the old shape. Defeats: DET-INF-018. Bad: the release removes `users.full_name` while the still-running old version reads it during the rollout, erroring every request it serves. Instead: expand in this release, contract in a later one after the old code is gone (DO-047). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-DO-021 — Deploy-history audit.** Verifies: DO-043, DO-044. Check: automated — script the deploy log/platform API for the last three production deploys; each must resolve to a commit SHA and an artifact digest, and the production digest must equal the digest that passed staging for that release. Pass: 3 of 3 resolve and match. Fail: block the next release until records exist. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-022 — Manual-step scan.** Verifies: DO-042. Check: automated — grep CI workflows, deploy scripts, and the runbook for `ftp `, `scp `, `rsync` to a production host, and `ssh` followed by `git pull` or a build command; deploy tooling that runs from CI off an artifact is exempt and must be annotated as such. Pass: zero unannotated hits. Fail: block shipment; the manual step is automated or the release does not go. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-023 — Switch and switch-back drill.** Verifies: DO-046, DO-050, DO-051. Check: manual, timed, in staging — run the blue-green/canary switch, exercise the written abort threshold, and switch back; the previous version must be serving again within the project's rollback target time. Pass: switch-back completes in target with the abort condition demonstrably triggered. Fail: the strategy is downgraded to rolling until the drill passes. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-024 — Production environment protection.** Verifies: DO-045. Check: automated where the platform API allows, else console inspection with a screenshot filed — the production environment has branch restrictions and its approval/pause rule enabled, and a test deploy from a non-protected branch is refused. Pass: refusal observed and rules present. Fail: block production deploys until protection is configured. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **The ceremonial canary.** One percent of traffic for five minutes, then full promotion because the clock ran out — no baseline comparison was ever made. Catch it: the canary record shows elapsed time but no error-rate or latency numbers against baseline.
- **Staging theater.** Staging runs a different artifact shape or hand-set config, so a green staging drill proves nothing about production. Catch it: diff the staging and production deploy specs; differences beyond env values are the tell.
- **The flag graveyard.** Feature flags are flipped on and never removed; six months later nobody can say which flags are live or safe to touch. Catch it: list flags older than one release cycle with no owner — each gets an owner and a removal date or is deleted.
- **Deploy by hero.** One person holds the deploy sequence in their head; releases wait for them and incidents wait longer. Catch it: a second operator (or the same operator, cold, from the runbook alone) must be able to run the deploy — if the runbook cannot carry it, the process is the hero.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Hand-carried deploy replaced by artifact promotion](examples/example-1.md) — corrects DO-042, DO-043.
- [Example 2 — Abort-free canary given metrics gates](examples/example-2.md) — corrects DO-046, DO-052.
- [Example 3 — Same-release column drop split into expand-and-contract](examples/example-3.md) — corrects DO-047.

## Recall anchors

- Build once; promote the same artifact everywhere.
- No hands on production: CI deploys, records prove it.
- No abort condition written down, no rollout.
- Expand now, contract later — old and new code coexist.
- The flag flip is the release; the flip back is the rollback.

## Checklist

- [ ] Strategy named for this change, with its risk reason, in the deploy record (DO-041).
- [ ] Deploy runs entirely from CI off the staging-passed digest — no manual steps (G-DO-022, DO-043).
- [ ] Deploy record holds digest, commit SHA, strategy, trigger, timestamp (DO-044).
- [ ] Production environment protection verified; non-protected-branch deploy refused (G-DO-024).
- [ ] Abort metric, threshold, and return action written before promotion (DO-046).
- [ ] Database changes are expand-only in this release; contract deferred (DO-047).
- [ ] Previous version still deployable until the observation window closes (DO-051).
- [ ] Last switch-back drill passed within the rollback target time (G-DO-023).

<!-- generated from skills/devops-deployment/domains-dns/SKILL.md -->

# domains-dns

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Cloudflare Docs, "DNS record types" — https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/
- **Depends on:** hosting
- **Feeds into:** ssl-certificates, cdn-strategy

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a domain is registered, transferred, or pointed at a host; any DNS record is created, changed, or removed; a migration moves a live domain between hosts; or mail starts sending from a domain.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is certificate issuance or renewal mechanics (ssl-certificates) or CDN caching and edge rules (cdn-strategy). This skill owns the records those skills depend on, not their internals.

## Rules

1. **DO-201 — The domain is an organizational asset.** The production domain is registered to the organization, or demonstrably recoverable by it, with auto-renew on, MFA on the registrar account, and the transfer lock on. A domain only one person can renew or recover fails this rule.
2. **DO-202 — Records carry intent.** Every record exists because a named service needs it, and the apex and `www` names point at the host's documented targets for this project. The intended zone is written down as a record sheet before records are created.
3. **DO-203 — No bare CNAME at the apex.** The apex name never holds a plain CNAME record, which conflicts with the other records the apex must carry. Use the provider's CNAME flattening, ALIAS, or ANAME mechanism, or the A/AAAA records the host documents.
4. **DO-204 — Lower TTL before a migration.** Before a planned change, lower the affected records' TTL (proxied Cloudflare records default to an automatic 300-second TTL, as of 2026-11); make the change after the old TTL has elapsed, verify, then raise the TTL again.
5. **DO-205 — Verify with `dig`, not the dashboard.** A change is verified by `dig +short` output against the authoritative nameservers matching the record sheet. A registrar dashboard's green checkmark is not verification.
6. **DO-206 — Mail records ship with the domain setup.** SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records are published before the domain sends mail, not after the first spam-folder incident.
7. **DO-207 — No record points at a dead or borrowed target.** No record targets a tutorial's example IP, a documentation placeholder, or a decommissioned host. A stale record is removed in the same change that replaces it.
8. **DO-208 — The zone is versioned or exported.** DNS is declared in IaC, or the zone is exported after every change and the export committed. The current state of the zone must be reconstructible from the repository alone.
9. **DO-209 — Expiry and lock status are monitored.** The domain's expiry date is recorded with an alert ahead of it, and auto-renew, MFA, and transfer-lock status are re-verified quarterly.
10. **DO-210 — "Propagation" is never a status.** A change is reported done only when `dig` against the authoritative nameservers returns the new value. A record that was never created is reported as never created, with the `dig` output as evidence.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-101 — Tutorial-copied records.** Banned: DNS records copied from a tutorial or blog post, including that post's example IP or hostname. Defeats: DET-INF-030. Bad: the apex A record points at the IP address printed in the setup tutorial the developer followed. Instead: take the target from the host's own documentation for this project, record it on the record sheet, and verify it with `dig +short`. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-102 — Bare CNAME at the apex.** Banned: a plain CNAME record on the apex/root name. Defeats: DET-INF-030. Bad: `@ CNAME app.hosting.example` is created and the apex MX and TXT records stop resolving. Instead: use CNAME flattening, ALIAS, or ANAME at the apex, or the A/AAAA records the host documents. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-103 — The personal-account domain.** Banned: a production domain held in a personal registrar account with no auto-renew, no MFA, and no recovery path for the organization. Defeats: DET-INF-030. Bad: the company domain sits on the founder's personal account and card; when the card expires, the domain lapses. Instead: hold the domain in the organization's account with auto-renew, MFA, and the transfer lock on. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-104 — "Still propagating" as an excuse.** Banned: reporting a DNS change as pending propagation when the record was never created or points at the wrong target. Defeats: DET-INF-030. Bad: the site is down for a day under the status "DNS is still propagating" while `dig` shows no A record exists at all. Instead: create the record, verify with `dig` against the authoritative nameservers, and report the actual `dig` output. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-DO-101 — Record-sheet match.** Verifies: DO-202, DO-205. Check: automated — run `dig +short <domain> A`, `dig +short www.<domain> CNAME`, and `dig +short www.<domain> A` after every change and quarterly; diff the output against the committed record sheet. Pass: every returned value matches the sheet exactly. Fail: block sign-off; correct the record or the sheet in the same change. Before a production environment is provisioned, this gate's disposition is a recorded provisioning waiver per the §6.3 protocol; it unblocks when a production domain is provisioned and its DNS records are live to query. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-102 — Registrar posture check.** Verifies: DO-201, DO-209. Check: manual registrar-console review with evidence (export or screenshot) covering account ownership, auto-renew, MFA, and transfer lock, plus the recorded expiry date and its alert. Pass: all four controls on and the expiry alert set. Fail: block launch until the posture is fixed. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-103 — Mail authentication present.** Verifies: DO-206. Check: automated — `dig +short <domain> TXT`, `dig +short <selector>._domainkey.<domain> TXT`, and `dig +short _dmarc.<domain> TXT` all return records before the domain sends mail. Pass: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records all resolve. Fail: block sending mail from the domain. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-104 — Zone export currency.** Verifies: DO-208. Check: compare the committed zone export (or IaC state) date against the date of the last DNS change recorded in progress.md. Pass: the export is the same age or newer than the last change. Fail: export the zone and commit it before sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Record sprawl.** Forgotten subdomains from old previews and experiments still resolve to dead services. Catch it by diffing the zone export against the record sheet at the quarterly check; a record nobody can name a service for is removed.
- **The imported zone.** A previous project's zone file is imported wholesale, including its service-verification TXT records for tools this project never uses. Catch it by reviewing every imported record against this project's record sheet before applying.
- **TTL left at migration value.** The 60-second TTL set for a migration is never raised afterward, leaving the zone permanently chatty and fragile. Catch it by making "TTL restored" the last line of every migration checklist.
- **Two sources of truth.** Some records live in the registrar panel and others in a DNS provider, and nobody is sure which zone is authoritative. Catch it by confirming the nameservers with `dig +short <domain> NS` and keeping exactly one authoritative zone.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Apex pointed with a bare CNAME](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects DO-203.
- [Example 2 — Migration done on hope and "propagation"](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects DO-204, DO-205, DO-210.
- [Example 3 — Mail sent before its records existed](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects DO-206.

## Recall anchors

- The domain belongs to the organization, never to a person's account.
- No bare CNAME at the apex — flatten, alias, or use A records.
- Lower TTL first, change, verify with `dig`, then raise TTL.
- `dig` output is verification; a dashboard checkmark is not.
- SPF, DKIM, and DMARC ship with the domain, not after the first incident.

## Checklist

- [ ] Domain held by the organization with auto-renew, MFA, and transfer lock verified with evidence (DO-201).
- [ ] Record sheet written, and apex plus `www` match it under `dig +short` (DO-202, DO-205).
- [ ] No bare CNAME at the apex; flattening/ALIAS or A/AAAA used instead (DO-203).
- [ ] Migration TTL lowered before the change and restored after verification (DO-204).
- [ ] SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records resolve before the domain sends mail (DO-206).
- [ ] No record points at a tutorial example, placeholder, or decommissioned host (DO-207).
- [ ] Current zone export or IaC state committed after the last change (DO-208).

<!-- generated from skills/devops-deployment/free-tiers/SKILL.md -->

# free-tiers

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://render.com/docs/free ; https://vercel.com/pricing ; https://www.netlify.com/pricing/ ; https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions
- **Depends on:** hosting
- **Feeds into:** cloud-costs, scaling, reliability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** any part of the stack (hosting, database, CI, CDN, storage) runs on a free tier or free plan, at launch or later; when a launch plan claims "$0 hosting"; when a free-tier limit is quoted in any plan, estimate, or client-facing document.
- **Do NOT use when:** the stack is fully paid — use cloud-costs for spend control instead. Do not use this skill to pick the host itself; that is hosting, which consumes this skill's free-tier sheet.

## Rules

1. **DO-161 — One sheet per stack.** Before launch, create a free-tier sheet in the project notes with one row per provider in the stack (hosting, database, CI, CDN, storage, email) and these fields per row: cap, behavior at the cap (hard stop or billing starts), sleep/expiry behavior, commercial-use terms, official limits-page URL, and date checked. A provider missing from the sheet fails G-DO-081.
2. **DO-162 — No unsourced numbers.** A tier limit, quota, or price appears in a plan only if it was read on the provider's official pricing/limits page and the sheet records that URL and the check date. Numbers from blog posts, videos, or memory are placeholders and are marked as such, never presented as limits.
3. **DO-163 — Entries expire after 90 days.** A sheet entry older than 90 days is stale; re-read the official page and update the entry before any launch, migration, or capacity decision that relies on it. Free tiers shrink with little notice, so the check date is part of the fact.
4. **DO-164 — Alert below every hard cap.** Where the provider offers usage alerts or quota notifications, set one below each hard cap (for example at 80% of the recorded cap) before launch, routed to a channel a named person reads. Where no alert exists, record that fact in the sheet and name the manual check that replaces it.
5. **DO-165 — Name the binding constraint.** For the whole stack, identify which cap is reached first at expected launch load and record it in the sheet as the binding constraint, with the expected symptom when it hits (downtime, failed builds, rejected requests). A launch plan that lists caps but no binding constraint is incomplete.
6. **DO-166 — Sleeping tiers are validation-only.** A tier that sleeps or spins down when idle (Render free web services spin down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic and take about a minute to spin back up, checked 2026-11-21) hosts demos and validation only — never a service with real users, inbound webhooks, or scheduled jobs that must fire on time.
7. **DO-167 — Record expiries the day they are created.** When a free resource has a lifetime (Render free PostgreSQL expires 30 days after creation, checked 2026-11-21), record its expiry date in the sheet on creation day and set a reminder before it. An expiry that falls inside the launch window with no migration plan is a launch blocker.
8. **DO-168 — Commercial work needs commercial terms.** Never run a production or revenue-bearing workload on a tier whose terms restrict it to personal or non-commercial use. Check the terms field of the sheet before launch; a mismatch means change the tier or the plan, not ignore the terms.
9. **DO-169 — Shared pools are summed, not per-service.** Where a quota is shared (Render's 750 free instance hours are per workspace per month, not per service, checked 2026-11-21), the sheet records the pool total and the sum of all services drawing on it. Planning each service against the full pool overstates capacity and fails G-DO-081.
10. **DO-170 — No state on ephemeral filesystems.** On tiers whose local filesystem is wiped on spin-down, redeploy, or restart (Render free behavior, checked 2026-11-21), uploads, sessions, and databases live in real external stores. Anything the app writes to local disk on such a tier is treated as disposable cache.
11. **DO-171 — Name the first paid step and its trigger in advance.** The sheet names, per provider, the first paid upgrade and the event that triggers it (first real user, first payment, cap forecast within 30 days). Per the project's $0-spend posture, no paid step is taken before its trigger fires; where a cap cannot be bought past at all (Vercel Hobby cannot purchase extra usage past its caps, as of 2026-11), hitting the cap means a plan change, and the sheet says so.
12. **DO-172 — Hard-stop and billing-start caps are different risks.** The sheet's at-cap behavior field distinguishes "service stops" from "billing starts." A billing-start cap on any provider requires a recorded spend decision (who approved overage, up to what amount) before launch; an unrecorded billing-start cap is an unbudgeted liability.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-081 — Invented tier limits.** Banned: stating a free-tier limit, quota, or price in a plan without an official page URL and check date in the sheet. Defeats: DET-INF-027 (nearest match — no DET parameter names this exact signal). Bad: "Render free gives 1,000 hours/month, plenty for launch" — a number from memory, 33% above the real shared pool. Instead: read https://render.com/docs/free, record the actual cap with the date checked, and mark anything unverified as a placeholder. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-082 — Sleeping tier in production.** Banned: pointing real users, production webhooks, or scheduled jobs at a tier that sleeps when idle. Defeats: DET-INF-019. Bad: the production API runs on a free tier that spins down after 15 idle minutes, so the first request each morning — and every payment webhook — waits ~1 minute or times out. Instead: keep sleeping tiers for demos and validation; production runs on an always-on tier or a recorded paid step per DO-171. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-083 — Expiring resource with no expiry record.** Banned: creating a free resource with a fixed lifetime and not recording its expiry date the same day. Defeats: DET-INF-008 (nearest match — no DET parameter names this exact signal). Bad: the free PostgreSQL instance is created at project start; 30 days later it expires mid-launch with the only copy of the data inside. Instead: record the expiry date in the sheet on creation day, set a reminder ahead of it, and name the migration or backup step that runs before it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-084 — Commercial production on a personal-use tier.** Banned: running a revenue-bearing production service on a tier whose terms allow personal or non-commercial use only. Defeats: DET-INF-019. Bad: the paid product's only deployment sits on a personal hobby tier because it is free; enforcement or a cap hit takes the whole business down with no fallback. Instead: verify the terms field before launch and move commercial production to a tier whose terms permit it, per DO-168. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-085 — Unrecorded billing-start cap.** Banned: launching on a tier where passing the cap starts metered billing, with no recorded spend decision. Defeats: DET-INF-027 (nearest match — no DET parameter names this exact signal). Bad: a traffic spike pushes the project past its free allowance and the first notice is an invoice nobody approved. Instead: record the at-cap behavior per DO-172 and, for billing-start caps, the approved overage decision — or choose a hard-stop tier. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-DO-081 — Free-tier sheet audit (automated).** Verifies: DO-161, DO-162, DO-163, DO-169. Check: `grep -c '^| ' docs/free-tier-sheet.md` equals the provider count in the stack list, and for every row, `grep -E 'Checked: [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}'` matches a date within the last 90 days (verify with `date -d`); each row contains cap, at-cap behavior, sleep/expiry, terms, and source URL fields. Pass: every provider in the stack has a complete row ≤90 days old, and shared pools show the summed draw. Fail: block launch until the sheet is complete and fresh. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-082 — Alert coverage check.** Verifies: DO-164. Check: for each hard cap in the sheet, open the provider console and confirm a usage alert exists below the cap routed to a monitored channel; where the provider offers none, confirm the sheet names the manual replacement check. Pass: every hard cap is covered by an alert or a named manual check. Fail: block launch. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-083 — Production posture check.** Verifies: DO-166, DO-168. Check: list every production workload and its tier from the sheet; confirm none runs on a sleeping tier or a personal/non-commercial-only tier. Pass: zero production workloads on sleeping or terms-mismatched tiers. Fail: block launch. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-084 — Expiry register check.** Verifies: DO-167. Check: for every sheet row with an expiry behavior, confirm an expiry date and a pre-expiry reminder exist, and no expiry falls inside the launch window without a recorded migration step. Pass: all expiries dated, reminded, and covered. Fail: block launch. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Headline-number planning.** Quoting the biggest number on a pricing page ("generous free bandwidth!") while the binding constraint is a smaller, quieter cap elsewhere in the stack. Catch it by asking which cap is hit first — if nobody can answer, DO-165 was skipped.
- **Screenshot sourcing.** Copying tier numbers from a blog post, video, or comparison table instead of the provider's own page; the numbers are often for a different plan or a past year. Catch it by checking every sheet row has an official-domain URL.
- **Free-stack sprawl.** Spreading one small app across six providers' free tiers to dodge a single cap, multiplying the sheets, alerts, and failure modes the project must track. Catch it by counting providers: each one must earn its place against the operational cost of tracking it.
- **Set-and-forget sheet.** Writing the free-tier sheet once at project start and never re-checking it, so the plan quietly runs on last year's limits. Catch it by sorting the sheet by check date — the oldest date is the plan's real freshness.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Invented limits in a launch plan](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects DO-162.
- [Example 2 — Sleeping tier chosen for a production API](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects DO-166.
- [Example 3 — Expiring free database with no expiry recorded](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects DO-167.

## Recall anchors

- No number without an official page and a check date.
- Sleeping tiers are for demos; expiring tiers are launch blockers.
- Shared pools are summed across every service, never per-service.
- Know the binding constraint and what happens when it hits.
- Name the first paid step and its trigger before you need it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Free-tier sheet exists with a complete row (cap, at-cap behavior, sleep/expiry, terms, URL, date) for every provider in the stack. (DO-161)
- [ ] Every limit in every plan traces to an official page checked within the last 90 days. (DO-162, DO-163)
- [ ] A usage alert sits below every hard cap, or a named manual check replaces it. (DO-164)
- [ ] The stack's binding constraint and its at-cap symptom are recorded. (DO-165, DO-172)
- [ ] No production workload runs on a sleeping tier or a personal/non-commercial-only tier. (DO-166, DO-168)
- [ ] Every expiring resource has its expiry date and a pre-expiry reminder recorded. (DO-167)
- [ ] Shared pools are recorded as pool totals with the summed draw of all services. (DO-169)
- [ ] The first paid upgrade and its trigger are named for each provider. (DO-171)

# hosting

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D6 DevOps & Deployment (DO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Netlify Docs, "Create deploys" — https://docs.Netlify.com/site-deploys/create-deploys ; Render Docs, "Deploy for Free" — https://render.com/docs/free ; OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html ; Cloudflare Docs, "Rate limiting rules" — https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/ ; Kubernetes Docs, liveness/readiness probes — https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/ ; AWS Well-Architected Reliability Pillar — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/welcome.html
- **Depends on:** infrastructure-as-code, deployment-strategies, free-tiers
- **Feeds into:** reliability, domains-dns, ssl-certificates, scaling

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** choosing or changing where a web application runs, promoting a deployment from validation to production use, or auditing an existing host against its recorded limits.
- **Do NOT use when:** deciding how a release is rolled out (deployment-strategies), accounting for a provider's free-tier caps in depth (free-tiers), or configuring DNS records and certificates themselves (domains-dns, ssl-certificates).

## Rules

1. **DO-141 — The host decision is recorded.** The hosting record names the provider and plan, region(s), scaling behavior, sleep policy, bandwidth and build caps, and the exit path, each with the date it was checked against the provider's own documentation. A host chosen without this record is not chosen yet.
2. **DO-142 — Every deployment carries a posture tier.** Each deployment is labeled validation posture or production posture in the hosting record. The record names the promotion trigger (first real user, first payment, first availability commitment) and lists which detection parameters are knowingly waived at validation posture.
3. **DO-143 — No unrecorded single point of failure.** A production-posture deployment with availability requirements does not run as a single instance with its database on the same host unless that risk is a recorded decision in the hosting record with a named exit path.
4. **DO-144 — Health checks reflect the ability to serve.** The app exposes a readiness endpoint that fails when a required dependency (database, cache, queue) is unreachable, and the platform's health check points at it. A probe aimed at the homepage or any static page does not satisfy this rule.
5. **DO-145 — Ephemeral filesystems hold no state.** On a platform whose filesystem is reset by redeploys or spin-downs, user uploads and the application database live in external stores (object storage, managed database), never in local files or a local database file.
6. **DO-146 — Platform config is the IaC of record.** The provider's config file (for example `netlify.toml`, `render.yaml`, `fly.toml`, `vercel.json`) is committed to the repo, and the console matches it. Any difference between console and committed config is drift and is reconciled the same day it is found.
7. **DO-147 — Debug and admin surfaces stay closed.** Production runs with framework debug mode off, error responses contain no stack traces, and `/.git`, `/.env`, admin, and metrics paths are unreachable publicly or sit behind authentication plus network restriction.
8. **DO-148 — Host defaults are hardened.** Directory listing is off, server and framework version banners are suppressed, default welcome pages and unused virtual hosts are removed, and only the ports the application needs are open.
9. **DO-149 — Auth endpoints are throttled at the edge.** Rate-limit rules at the CDN, WAF, or gateway cover login, password-reset, and signup paths before launch, with stricter limits for unauthenticated traffic.
10. **DO-150 — Production is a separate environment.** Production has its own data store and its own credentials; staging and production resolve to different database hosts, and production data is never the test fixture.
11. **DO-151 — Production is verified from outside.** After every deploy, the public production URL is loaded over valid HTTPS from a network other than the deploy network, and the live deployment's commit SHA is confirmed equal to the repo HEAD and written into progress.md.
12. **DO-152 — The host-limit sheet stays current.** Caps that can stop the app (sleep behavior, bandwidth, build minutes, instance hours, expiring resources such as free databases) are recorded with their expiry or reset dates and re-checked against provider documentation at least every 90 days.

## BAN list

- **BAN-DO-071 — The localhost launch.** Banned: declaring an app launched from a localhost screenshot or a provider's "deployed" badge without an external check of the public URL. Defeats: DET-INF-003. Bad: the launch is announced with a screenshot of localhost:3000 while the production URL still serves the placeholder page. Instead: load the public production URL from a second network over HTTPS and record the live commit SHA before calling anything launched. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-072 — The unrecorded single box.** Banned: running a production deployment as one instance with its database on the same host, with no recorded risk decision and no exit path. Defeats: DET-INF-019. Bad: one VPS runs the app and its PostgreSQL; a single disk failure takes the product and its data down together, and nobody ever wrote the risk down. Instead: move the database to a managed store or separate host, or record the accepted risk and its exit path in the hosting record. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-073 — The homepage health check.** Banned: pointing the platform health check at the homepage or a static page that cannot fail. Defeats: DET-INF-020. Bad: the probe hits `/`, which returns 200 from cache while the database is down, so the platform never restarts or drains the broken instance. Instead: expose a readiness endpoint that checks the app's dependencies and point the platform probe at it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-074 — Debug shipped to production.** Banned: deploying with framework debug mode enabled, or with `/.git` or `/.env` reachable on the public host. Defeats: DET-INF-021. Bad: the development config is copied to production verbatim, and an error page shows visitors a full stack trace with file paths. Instead: disable debug by environment configuration in production and block the sensitive paths at the host. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-DO-075 — Unthrottled auth at launch.** Banned: launching on a host with no edge rate limit on login, password-reset, or signup endpoints. Defeats: DET-INF-023. Bad: credential stuffing runs against the login form at full speed because the only throttle is application code written for the happy path. Instead: add CDN/WAF or gateway rate-limit rules for the auth paths before launch. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-DO-071 — External production check.** Verifies: DO-151, DO-141. Check: automated — `curl -sI https://<production-domain>/` from a network other than the deploy network returns 200 over a valid certificate, and the provider's deployment record shows a commit SHA equal to `git rev-parse HEAD`. Pass: both true. Fail: block the launch or release announcement until both hold. Before a production environment is provisioned, this gate's disposition is a recorded provisioning waiver per the §6.3 protocol; it unblocks when a production domain is provisioned and the release is deployed to it. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-072 — Readiness honesty test.** Verifies: DO-144. Check: automated — in staging, stop the database (or block its port), then confirm the readiness endpoint returns a non-200 status within 60 seconds while the liveness endpoint still returns 200. Pass: readiness fails and liveness passes. Fail: block promotion to production posture. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-073 — Exposure probe.** Verifies: DO-147, DO-148. Check: automated — `for p in /.git/HEAD /.env /phpinfo; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $p\n" https://<production-domain>$p; done` returns only 403 or 404, and `curl -sI https://<production-domain>/` shows no version-bearing `Server:` or `X-Powered-By` header. Pass: all probes blocked and no version banners. Fail: block shipment. Before a production environment is provisioned, this gate's disposition is a recorded provisioning waiver per the §6.3 protocol; it unblocks when a production domain is provisioned and the deployed release can be probed from an external network. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-074 — Config-drift diff.** Verifies: DO-146. Check: semi-automated — export the provider console settings and diff them against the committed platform config file (build command, environment variable names, region, instance count). Pass: zero unexplained differences. Fail: reconcile the same day; drift surviving one release blocks the next deploy. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-DO-075 — Hosting record audit.** Verifies: DO-141, DO-142, DO-143, DO-152. Check: manual — open the hosting record and confirm provider, region, scaling behavior, sleep policy, caps, exit path, posture tier, any single-point-of-failure decision, and a check date no more than 90 days old are all present. Pass: every field present and current. Fail: block promotion to production posture. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **The generous free tier.** The host is picked because its free tier "should be enough"; the binding cap is discovered at the first traffic spike. Catch it: the host-limit sheet names the binding cap and what happens when it is hit, before launch (DO-152).
- **Sleep-blind scheduling.** Webhooks, cron jobs, or background workers are placed on a host that spins down when idle, so they silently stop firing. Catch it: check the record's sleep policy against every scheduled and webhook dependency before wiring them up.
- **Region by default.** The app runs in whatever region the provider defaulted to, far from both its users and its database. Catch it: app region and database region are both named in the hosting record, and they match.
- **Dashboard truth.** The provider dashboard is treated as the record of what is live; nobody can say which commit is running without opening it. Catch it: the live commit SHA is written into progress.md at every deploy (G-DO-071).

## Examples

- [Example 1 — A localhost "launch" replaced by an externally verified deployment](examples/example-1.md) — corrects DO-151.
- [Example 2 — A single-box deployment recorded, then promoted](examples/example-2.md) — corrects DO-143.
- [Example 3 — A static-page probe replaced by a real readiness check](examples/example-3.md) — corrects DO-144.

## Recall anchors

- Pick the host by workload shape; write its limits down.
- Production is proven from outside, on the current commit.
- Readiness checks dependencies; a static page proves nothing.
- Ephemeral disk holds no state — uploads and data live in real stores.
- Console and committed config match, or it is drift.

## Checklist

- [ ] Hosting record is complete: provider, region, scaling, sleep policy, caps, exit path, check date (DO-141).
- [ ] Posture tier is declared, with its promotion trigger and waived parameters (DO-142).
- [ ] No unrecorded single point of failure in production posture (DO-143, G-DO-075).
- [ ] Readiness fails in staging when the database is stopped (G-DO-072).
- [ ] Exposure probes are blocked and no version banners are served (G-DO-073).
- [ ] External check passes and the live commit SHA equals repo HEAD (G-DO-071).
- [ ] Console settings diff clean against the committed platform config (G-DO-074).
