<!-- generated from skills/qa-testing/unit-testing/SKILL.md -->

# unit-testing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.martinfowler.com/articles/practical-test-pyramid.html
- **Depends on:** test-strategy
- **Feeds into:** qa-gates, integration-testing

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** writing or reviewing tests for a single module, function, or class — pricing math, validation, parsing, state transitions, permission checks — that can be proven without a database, network, or browser.
- **Do NOT use when:** the behavior only exists across real collaborators (database, HTTP layer, another service) — use integration-testing; or across a full user journey — use e2e-testing. Do not stretch a unit test into either by mocking the collaborators away.

## Rules

1. **QA-001 — One test file per module, fast runner, first job.** Each module has a matching test file run by the stack's fast runner (Vitest, pytest, JUnit); the unit suite is the first CI job and finishes within the wall-time budget in TESTING.md.
2. **QA-002 — Every test asserts a specific expected value.** A test states the exact output, state, or side effect it expects. A test whose only assertion is "does not throw" is labeled a smoke test and never counts toward coverage of logic.
3. **QA-003 — Tests are isolated and order-independent.** Each test arranges its own inputs; no shared mutable fixtures, no reliance on another test's leftovers. The suite passes with tests shuffled and with any single test run alone.
4. **QA-004 — No real network, database, filesystem, or wall-clock.** Time and randomness are injected as parameters or fakes controlled by the test; a unit test that sleeps, reads the real clock, or opens a socket is defective.
5. **QA-005 — Assert behavior, not implementation.** Assert on return values and observable side effects, never on private internals or call-by-call mock choreography that a behavior-preserving refactor would break.
6. **QA-006 — Doubles live at the unit boundary only.** External collaborators (payment API, email sender) may be replaced by test doubles; the unit under test and the project's own modules are never doubled.
7. **QA-007 — A bug fix lands with its failing test.** The regression test is written first or in the same commit as the fix, so the bug is permanently pinned; a fix with no test is incomplete work.
8. **QA-008 — Coverage is a floor signal, not a target.** Coverage exists to expose untested code. Uncovered branches in money, auth, and data-loss paths are closed first; a coverage percentage is never reported as proof of quality on its own.
9. **QA-009 — The suite must be able to fail.** Mutating one assertion's expected value in a core module — or running a mutation-testing sample on core modules — must turn the suite red; a suite that stays green under mutation is reopened as a defect.
10. **QA-010 — Flaky unit tests are defects, not weather.** A test that passes on re-run without a code change is quarantined with an owner and expiry date, or fixed; silent retries that launder intermittency into green are not permitted at this layer.

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-001 — Assertion-free coverage gaming.** Banned: a test that executes the code under test and asserts nothing (or only that no exception was thrown) while counting toward logic coverage. Defeats: DET-CODE-012. Bad: `test("totals", () => { cart.total(); });` — the frozen-fixture dashboard passes this test forever. Instead: assert the exact expected total for named inputs, e.g. `expect(cart.total()).toBe(4200)`. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-002 — Doubling the unit under test.** Banned: mocking or stubbing the module being tested, or a hand-written fake of the project's own logic, so the test verifies the double's canned answers. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Bad: search tests stub `search()` itself to return a fixed result list, then "verify" ranking. Instead: run the real unit; double only the external index client at the boundary. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-003 — Tautological fixture assertion.** Banned: asserting that the code returns the same hardcoded constant the implementation itself contains, so test and code can be wrong together. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Bad: implementation returns seed user `"admin@example.com"`; test asserts the return equals `"admin@example.com"` copied from the seed. Instead: compute the expectation independently in the test (from the rule or a worked example) and assert against that. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-004 — Disabling a failing test to go green.** Banned: `.skip`, `xit`, commented-out assertions, or a deleted test used to make the suite pass without a fix or a tracked quarantine (owner + expiry, per QA-010). Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Bad: `test.skip("rejects expired token")` committed with the note "fix later," suite reported green. Instead: fix the code or the test; if neither is possible now, quarantine it as a tracked defect with an owner and expiry date, and report the suite as carrying a known failure. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-QA-001 — Seeded-fault (mutation) gate.** Verifies: QA-002, QA-009. Check: in CI, run `scripts/mutation-spotcheck.sh` — it flips one expected value in a core-module test (or runs the mutation sample), runs the unit suite, and requires a non-zero exit; it then restores the file and requires exit 0. Pass: suite exits non-zero under mutation and 0 after restore. Fail: block merge; the hollow test is a defect. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-QA-002 — Isolation and shuffle gate.** Verifies: QA-003. Check: CI runs the suite twice — `npm test -- --sequence.shuffle` (Vitest) / `pytest -p no:cacheprovider --random-order` equivalent for the stack — and once per test file in isolation; all runs must exit 0. Pass: every run exits 0. Fail: block merge; the order-dependent test is fixed, not re-run until green. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-QA-003 — Assertion-presence gate.** Verifies: QA-002. Check: CI runs `scripts/check-assertions.sh`, which scans unit test files and exits 1 if any test body contains no assertion call (`expect(`, `assert`, `should`) and is not labeled `smoke`. Pass: script exits 0. Fail: block merge until each flagged test asserts a specific value or is relabeled smoke. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-QA-004 — Wall-time budget gate.** Verifies: QA-001. Check: the CI unit job declares a timeout equal to the budget in TESTING.md (config inspection: `grep -n "timeout" .github/workflows/*.yml` shows the value); the platform kills and fails the job on breach. Pass: timeout present and the job completes inside it. Fail: block merge; slow tests are profiled and pushed down or fixed, never absorbed by raising the timeout without a TESTING.md change. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Snapshot everything.** Giant snapshots nobody reads, regenerated with `--update` whenever they fail — the diff is the test, and approving it unread deletes the test. Catch it: a snapshot update in a PR with no explanation of the intended change.
- **Test-name theater.** Names promise behavior the body never checks: `rejects expired token` that only exercises a valid token. Catch it: read the body against the name before reading the result.
- **Slow creep.** Unit tests quietly boot the framework, open connections, and load fixtures until the "fast" job takes twenty minutes and developers stop running it locally. Catch it: the suite's wall time trends up across releases while test count barely moves.
- **Copy-paste suites.** The same test block duplicated across modules, drifting apart until half the copies assert stale behavior. Catch it: near-identical test bodies in three or more files with different expectations.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Assertion-free test becomes a real assertion](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects QA-002.
- [Example 2 — Shared mutable fixture becomes isolated arrange](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects QA-003.
- [Example 3 — Wall-clock dependency becomes injected time](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects QA-004.

## Recall anchors

- A test that cannot fail is decoration, not proof.
- Assert a value, not a vibe: exact expectation or it is a smoke test.
- Shuffle it, run it alone — isolation is part of the test.
- Double the boundary, never the unit.
- Coverage finds untested code; it never proves tested code is right.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every test asserts a specific expected value, or is labeled smoke (QA-002).
- [ ] Suite passes shuffled and with each test file run alone (QA-003, G-QA-002).
- [ ] No real network, database, filesystem, or wall-clock access in any unit test (QA-004).
- [ ] Doubles exist only at external boundaries; the unit under test runs for real (QA-006).
- [ ] Any bug fixed in this change has its failing test in the same commit (QA-007).
- [ ] Seeded-fault gate ran and the suite went red under mutation (G-QA-001).
- [ ] No skipped or disabled tests without a tracked owner and expiry date (QA-010).

<!-- generated from skills/qa-testing/visual-regression/SKILL.md -->

# visual-regression

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots
- **Depends on:** test-strategy, browser-verification
- **Feeds into:** qa-gates

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a project has pages or component states where layout is the product — marketing pages, dashboards, checkout, email-critical screens — and layout drift must fail a pull request mechanically.
- **Do NOT use when:** the check is behavioral rather than visual (use e2e-testing or browser-verification), or the surface is a native app or canvas game with no stable rendered layout (use manual review and record why in TESTING.md).

## Rules

1. **QA-081 — Pinned environment.** Baselines are generated and compared inside one pinned environment — same container image, browser build, and font set — and the image digest and browser version are recorded in the test config. A baseline produced on a developer machine is invalid.
2. **QA-082 — Baselines change only by reviewed PR.** A baseline file changes only in a pull request whose description names the intentional design change it accepts. Regenerating baselines inside a feature PR without that statement is a process violation, however green it makes the run.
3. **QA-083 — Coverage by inventory.** Every template in the page/state inventory carries at least three screenshots: default, empty, and error state. The inventory comes from the design system, not from which pages someone remembered.
4. **QA-084 — Mask dynamics, never widen tolerance.** Timestamps, avatars, ads, and other dynamic regions are masked in the test that captures them. The global pixel threshold stays at the small value set in TESTING.md; raising it requires a waiver recorded per qa-gates.
5. **QA-085 — Animations frozen.** Screenshot tests run with animations disabled (`animations: "disabled"` in the screenshot assertion), so motion can never become flake.
6. **QA-086 — Diff artifact before re-run.** A failing comparison uploads the expected, actual, and diff images as CI artifacts. Triage opens the diff image first; re-running the job before reading the diff is not triage.
7. **QA-087 — Viewports match the support matrix.** The screenshot set covers every viewport class in the project's support matrix, including one mobile width; a desktop-only suite is reported as desktop-only coverage.
8. **QA-088 — Seeded-change negative control.** On a schedule, a throwaway branch shifts a header by 20px and the visual job must fail with a diff artifact. A job that passes the seeded change is itself a defect and blocks release until fixed.
9. **QA-089 — Baseline-drift report per release.** Each release produces a count of baselines changed since the previous release tag. Mass changes with no matching design-change statement block the release.
10. **QA-090 — Environment changes are single events.** A font or browser-version upgrade is one deliberate, repo-wide baseline regeneration in its own PR — never a per-test fix scattered across feature PRs.
11. **QA-091 — Compare the built artifact.** Comparisons run in CI against the pull request's built application, with the build SHA recorded beside the results — never against a locally rendered dev server.
12. **QA-092 — Quarantine expires.** A screenshot test that flakes twice in a week is quarantined with a ticket and an expiry date, and the quarantine count is reported per release. Deleting the test or silently retrying it away is forbidden.

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-041 — Baseline regeneration to green.** Banned: running the update-snapshots command to make a red visual run pass without a reviewed PR naming the design change. Defeats: DET-VIS-007. Bad: a spacing regression ships because the developer regenerated baselines in the same PR and the diff was never seen. Instead: keep the failure, open a baseline-only PR whose description states the intentional change, and let a reviewer read the diff images. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-042 — Threshold inflation.** Banned: raising the global pixel threshold or diff ratio to absorb failures instead of masking the dynamic region causing them. Defeats: DET-VIS-001. Bad: `maxDiffPixelRatio` raised to 0.25 so a timestamp stops failing — and a 12px padding collapse now passes too. Instead: mask the timestamp element in that one test and return the threshold to the value in TESTING.md. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-043 — Desktop-only coverage.** Banned: a visual suite whose viewports are all desktop widths while the support matrix includes mobile. Defeats: DET-VIS-038. Bad: the suite is green for months while the pricing table overflows horizontally on a 390px phone. Instead: add the mobile viewport from the support matrix to every inventory template's screenshot set. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-044 — Live-animation screenshots.** Banned: capturing screenshots while CSS animations or transitions run, so pass/fail depends on frame timing. Defeats: DET-VIS-040. Bad: the hero test flakes every few runs because the fade-up animation is mid-flight in half the captures. Instead: set `animations: "disabled"` on the screenshot assertion so every capture is the settled frame. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-045 — Default-state-only coverage.** Banned: screenshotting only the populated default state of a template, with no empty or error state. Defeats: DET-VIS-032. Bad: the dashboard's empty state renders its heading overlapped by the CTA, and no baseline exists to catch it. Instead: add the empty and error states from the inventory to the screenshot set before merging the template. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-QA-041 — Visual suite exit code.** Verifies: QA-081, QA-083, QA-085, QA-087. Check: `npx playwright test --grep @visual` in the pinned CI image. Pass: exit code 0 and the run report lists every inventory template with its default, empty, and error screenshots. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-QA-042 — Seeded-change control.** Verifies: QA-088. Check: the scheduled job applies a 20px header shift on a throwaway branch, runs `npx playwright test --grep @visual`, and asserts a non-zero exit plus a diff image in the artifacts. Pass: job fails as designed and the artifact exists. Fail: block release; the visual suite is treated as non-functional. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-QA-043 — Baseline-drift gate.** Verifies: QA-082, QA-089. Check: `git diff --name-only <last-release-tag>..HEAD -- '*-snapshots'` counts changed baselines; the release checklist requires a design-change statement for the count. Pass: every changed baseline traces to a reviewed baseline PR. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-QA-044 — Threshold config audit.** Verifies: QA-084. Check: `grep -Rn "maxDiffPixelRatio" --include="*.ts" .` and compare each value against the cap in TESTING.md. Pass: no value exceeds the cap and no per-test threshold overrides exist without a waiver reference. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Bulk diff approval.** Approving a stack of baseline changes from thumbnail previews without opening a single full-size diff image; catch it by sampling three diffs at full size before approving any baseline PR.
- **Retry-as-fix.** Letting CI retries absorb a flaky screenshot test until the quarantine rule (QA-092) never triggers; catch it by reading first-attempt results, not final status, in the weekly flake count.
- **Stale baseline hoarding.** Baselines for deleted pages and renamed components still sitting in the repo, inflating drift counts and hiding real changes; catch it in the per-release drift report by listing baselines whose routes no longer exist.
- **Marketing-page tourism.** Forty screenshots of the landing page and none of the settings, billing, or error surfaces users actually hit; catch it by diffing the screenshot list against the page/state inventory, not against page traffic.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Baseline regeneration to green](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects QA-082.
- [Example 2 — Threshold raised instead of masking](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects QA-084.
- [Example 3 — Desktop-only suite misses mobile overflow](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects QA-087.

## Recall anchors

- Baselines are reviewed diffs, not generated files.
- Mask the dynamic region; never widen the threshold.
- If a 20px shift passes, the suite is broken, not the page.
- Triage reads the diff image before anyone re-runs anything.
- A font or browser bump is one baseline event, not fifty fixes.

## Checklist

- [ ] Baselines were generated inside the pinned CI image, with its digest recorded (QA-081).
- [ ] Every baseline change sits in a reviewed PR naming the intentional design change (QA-082).
- [ ] Default, empty, and error states exist for every inventory template (QA-083).
- [ ] Dynamic regions are masked and the global threshold matches TESTING.md (QA-084).
- [ ] Animations are disabled in every screenshot assertion (QA-085).
- [ ] The latest seeded-change control failed the job and produced a diff artifact (QA-088).
- [ ] The release baseline-drift count is produced and explained (QA-089).
- [ ] No quarantined visual test is past its expiry date (QA-092).

# aeo

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735 ; https://www.kevinleary.net/blog/llms-txt-myth/ ; https://www.getdigitize.com/blog/llms-txt-for-brands/ ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, on-page-seo, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** geo, copywriting, structured-data, web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a page should be liftable by an answer engine — featured snippets, voice answers, Google AI Overviews / AI Mode — or when an AEO plan, tactic, or result is being written, reviewed, or reported.
- **Do NOT use when:** the problem is crawlability or indexation (use technical-seo), page intent and metadata (use on-page-seo), citation inside synthesized multi-source answers as a program (use geo), or markup implementation (use structured-data).

## Rules

1. **CO-041 — Answer first, self-contained.** The passage that answers the query sits at the top of its section and is true and complete when lifted alone: no "as mentioned above", no pronoun whose antecedent lives in another paragraph, no fact that needs the surrounding page to make sense.
2. **CO-042 — Question-shaped headings for question queries.** Where the target query is a question, the heading states that question in the searcher's wording and the answer passage follows it immediately; statements and procedures use descriptive headings instead.
3. **CO-043 — Extractable formats for extractable facts.** Procedural steps go in ordered lists, comparisons in tables, and definitions in a single sentence followed by expansion — formats that survive extraction intact.
4. **CO-044 — One canonical statement of every fact.** A fact used in an answer passage is stated once, in one canonical wording, and matches fact-sheet.md exactly; answer engines amplify contradictions, so a second wording of the same fact anywhere on the site is a defect (DET-CON-015 discipline).
5. **CO-045 — One version of the content.** The same page serves people and engines. No separate "AI version", no answer text hidden from users, no engine-only variant of a passage.
6. **CO-046 — AI-feature eligibility is ordinary Search eligibility (Documented).** For Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, a page must be indexed and eligible to appear in Search with a snippet; Google states there are no additional technical requirements, no special optimizations, and no special schema.org markup. Any plan claiming a further Google requirement must cite the Google page that states it.
7. **CO-047 — Every tactic carries an evidence-level tag.** Each AEO tactic in a plan, audit, or report is labeled Documented (platform-stated), Peer-reviewed (with the study's limits), Correlational (vendor/observational), or Hype (unsupported or contradicted). An untagged tactic fails review.
8. **CO-048 — llms.txt is hygiene, never a result (Hype if claimed otherwise).** llms.txt is a 2024 proposal, not an adopted standard; Google has stated on the record that it does not use the file, and a study of nearly 300,000 domains found no correlation with LLM citation frequency. The file may be shipped, but it is never reported as an AI-visibility win and never described as a Google-endorsed ranking factor.
9. **CO-049 — Crawler access is verified at every layer.** AI and search crawlers allowed in robots.txt must also pass the CDN, firewall, and hosting layer; Google's AI-features guidance names CDN/hosting blocking as a real eligibility failure, so access is tested with the crawler's user agent, not assumed.
10. **CO-050 — Answer-supporting structured data matches the visible text.** Any markup behind an answer (FAQ, HowTo, product facts) is generated from the same data as the rendered page and agrees with it field for field (DET-CON-024).
11. **CO-051 — Citability additions are sourced or absent (Peer-reviewed, limited).** Adding citations, quotations, and statistics is the one tactic with peer-reviewed support for raising visibility in generated answers (Aggarwal et al., KDD '24, GEO-bench, 2023-era models — an upper-bound result, not an average). Every added statistic or quotation must trace to a real source record under the real-content rule; an invented figure is a DET-CON-011 blocker even if it earns citations.
12. **CO-052 — Answer presence is measured on a fixed query set.** A written set of target queries is checked on a monthly cadence in AI Overviews and featured snippets, with date, engine, and citing URL logged. One screenshot of one answer is an anecdote, never a reported result.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-021 — llms.txt sold as a ranking factor.** Banned: presenting llms.txt (or any "AI text file") as a Google-endorsed ranking factor, a requirement for AI Overviews, or a measured visibility result. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; governed by CO-048. Bad: client report reads "Implemented llms.txt — expected to improve AI Overview citations." Instead: ship the file as hygiene if wanted and report it as such, tagged Hype/contradicted per CO-048, citing Google's on-record statements. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-022 — Separate or hidden AI-only content.** Banned: an engine-facing version of a page, or answer passages hidden from users (display:none, off-screen, crawler-only rendering) that differ from what users read. Defeats: DET-CON-024. Bad: the crawler receives a keyword-rich FAQ block that never renders for visitors. Instead: one page serves both — write the answer into the visible content (CO-045). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-023 — Fabricated citation bait.** Banned: inventing a statistic, quotation, or study result to make a passage more citable by answer engines. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Bad: "Studies show 87% of teams ship faster with checklists" with no study behind it. Instead: cite a real, producible source or delete the figure (CO-051). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-024 — Templated answer-page matrix.** Banned: stamping out one thin Q&A page per query variant with swapped keywords and no page-specific substance, to capture answer placements at scale. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Bad: 60 pages answering "best X for Y" from one skeleton, differing only in the product name. Instead: one canonical answer page per topic, expanded only with verified page-specific material. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-025 — Contradictory canonical answers.** Banned: two pages (or a page and its markup) stating different values for the same fact an engine might lift — prices, limits, dates, counts. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Bad: the pricing page says "50 GB included" while the FAQ answer says "100 GB included". Instead: state the fact once, from fact-sheet.md, and link rather than restate (CO-044). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-021 — Evidence-tag audit.** Verifies: CO-047, CO-048. Check: manual review of the AEO plan/report — every tactic line carries one of the four evidence tags, and no llms.txt or "AI file" line is tagged Documented or reported as a result. Pass: 100% of tactics tagged, zero hype presented as fact. Fail: return the plan for re-tagging before any work ships. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-022 — Answer-presence log.** Verifies: CO-052. Check: monthly — run the fixed target-query set, record date, surface (AI Overview / featured snippet / none), and the citing URL in the log; compare against the previous month. Pass: log entry complete for every query in the set. Fail: the month's AEO reporting is marked unmeasured, not estimated. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-023 — Passage self-containment and fact diff.** Verifies: CO-041, CO-044. Check: automated assist — grep answer sections for cross-reference dependencies: `grep -rniE 'as mentioned above|see above|as noted earlier|the aforementioned' content/` returns nothing; then diff every checkable fact in answer passages against fact-sheet.md. Pass: zero cross-references, zero fact mismatches. Fail: rewrite the passage before release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-024 — Crawler access test.** Verifies: CO-049. Check: automated — request key pages with the search crawler's user agent and assert a 200 with full content: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -A "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)" https://example.com/pricing` returns `200`, and robots.txt shows no Disallow for the path. Pass: 200 and no block at CDN, firewall, or robots layer. Fail: fix the blocking layer before claiming AEO eligibility. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-025 — Answer markup match.** Verifies: CO-050. Check: automated — parse each page's JSON-LD and diff answer-relevant fields (FAQ answers, prices, ratings) against the rendered text. Pass: every field has an identical visible counterpart. Fail: regenerate the markup from page data or remove it. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Snippet lottery rewrites.** Rewriting the answer passage after every monthly check, so no version is ever live long enough to measure; catch it by dating passage changes in the log and requiring a full measurement cycle between edits.
- **Answer bloat.** Padding the answer passage with background until the direct answer is no longer liftable; catch it by reading the first two sentences alone — if they don't answer the query, cut.
- **Vendor-metric reporting.** Quoting a tool's "AI visibility score" as if it were a platform metric; catch it at report review — every number must name its source and evidence level (CO-047).
- **Heading stuffing for questions.** Forcing every H2 into question form, including statements and procedures; catch it by checking each question heading against a real query — no query, no question heading (CO-042).

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Answer passage made self-contained](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects CO-041, CO-042.
- [Example 2 — llms.txt reported as a win, corrected with evidence tags](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects CO-047, CO-048.
- [Example 3 — Citation bait replaced with a sourced statistic](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects CO-051.

## Recall anchors

- Answer first, and make the answer stand alone when lifted.
- For Google AI features there is no separate discipline: indexed + snippet-eligible is the whole requirement.
- Tag every tactic: Documented, Peer-reviewed, Correlational, or Hype.
- llms.txt is hygiene, never a result — Google does not use it.
- A fact an engine can lift is stated once, canonically, from the fact sheet.

## Checklist

- [ ] Each target passage answers its query in its first sentences and stands alone when lifted (CO-041, G-CO-023).
- [ ] Question headings match real queries; procedures and comparisons use lists and tables (CO-042, CO-043).
- [ ] Every fact in an answer passage matches fact-sheet.md, stated in one canonical wording (CO-044).
- [ ] No AI-only or hidden content variant exists (CO-045).
- [ ] Every tactic in the plan/report carries an evidence-level tag; llms.txt is not claimed as a result (CO-047, CO-048, G-CO-021).
- [ ] Crawler access verified at robots, CDN, and hosting layers (CO-049, G-CO-024).
- [ ] Answer-supporting structured data matches the visible text field for field (CO-050, G-CO-025).
- [ ] This month's fixed-query answer-presence log is complete (CO-052, G-CO-022).

# content-strategy

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Mailchimp, content planning guide — https://mailchimp.com/resources/content-planning/ ; Google Search spam policies (scaled content abuse) — https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies ; Google Search Central, "Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content" — https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content ; Google Search Central Blog, "Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content" — https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/02/google-search-and-ai-content
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet, web-analytics
- **Feeds into:** copywriting, on-page-seo, real-content, internal-linking

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** deciding what content a site will produce, in what order, for whom, and to what end — topic maps, editorial calendars, briefs, and refresh/retire decisions. This skill owns the production system: strategy sets audience, goals, and topic ownership before any drafting starts.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is how a single page is written (copywriting), how its metadata is set (on-page-seo), or whether a specific factual element is evidenced (real-content — that gate runs at publish time and its blocker list outranks any plan made here). Never use strategy to justify volume the evidence cannot support.

## Rules

1. **CO-081 — No brief, no draft.** Every piece of content starts from a brief naming its audience, goal, target query or intent, owner, and reviewer. A brief missing any of the five does not enter production, and no draft is written against an unwritten brief.
2. **CO-082 — Volume is an output, never a quota.** The plan never sets a pages-per-week or pages-per-month target. Output is whatever number of briefs clear the CO-081 bar; Google's scaled content abuse policy makes volume-for-rankings the violation regardless of whether humans or AI wrote the pages.
3. **CO-083 — One canonical page per topic.** The topic map assigns each topic to exactly one canonical page. A second page on the same topic is admitted only with a written differentiation: a different audience, format, or body of page-specific verified material the canonical page does not carry.
4. **CO-084 — The swap test for variants.** A location, keyword, or product variant page ships only with real page-specific data (staff, stock, pricing, regulations, local facts) such that swapping the keyword back would break the page. If two variants stay interchangeable after the swap, they are one page, not two.
5. **CO-085 — Every piece carries an owner and a review-by date.** At publication, each page records a named owner and the date by which its claims are re-verified. A page with no owner or no review-by date is not finished, however polished the copy.
6. **CO-086 — Authorship is real.** Pieces are credited to real people the publisher can evidence, or to an accountable house byline ("The Support Team"). Invented author personas — names, headshots, bios for people who do not exist — are never planned, briefed, or published.
7. **CO-087 — Decisions cite data.** Every brief, refresh, and retirement names the evidence behind it: Search Console query/page data, analytics landing-page evidence, or a documented audience need. "We should write about X" with no cited evidence is an opinion, and opinions do not enter the calendar.
8. **CO-088 — Topics stay inside the real offer.** The topic map covers only subjects the business can actually serve and evidence from its own operation. A topic the business has no product, service, data, or experience behind is out of scope, however much search demand it shows.
9. **CO-089 — Refresh or retire on schedule.** When a page's review-by date arrives, its owner re-verifies its claims and then refreshes, retires, or re-dates it with the verification recorded. Silently editing the date without re-verifying the content is not a refresh.
10. **CO-090 — The programmatic admission bar.** Templated or programmatic page sets are admitted only when every page in the set carries page-specific verified data passing CO-084. A set whose pages differ only in a swapped term is rejected at planning, not discovered at audit.
11. **CO-091 — Distribution is part of the brief.** A brief is incomplete until it names the page's planned inbound internal links and its distribution step (newsletter, social, partner, in-product). A page planned to be found "by the sitemap" is planned to be orphaned.
12. **CO-092 — Depth per topic over page count.** When a topic cannot support another substantively different page, the plan deepens the canonical page — new verified data, better coverage of the intent — instead of spawning a sibling. The plan records this choice so the refusal of volume is a decision on file, not an omission.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-041 — Volume-quota planning.** Banned: setting a content target in pages per week/month, or back-filling a calendar to hit a count. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Bad: the Q3 plan commits to "120 location pages in 6 weeks" before anyone asks what each page would say. Instead: plan briefs that clear CO-081 and let the count be whatever survives; depth per topic (CO-092) absorbs the remaining effort. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-042 — Template-stamped page sets.** Banned: approving a set of pages built from one skeleton with keywords swapped per page. Defeats: DET-CON-008. Bad: forty "Best plumber in {city}" pages share identical headings and paragraph order; only the city name and a stock photo change. Instead: admit only variants carrying real local data that passes the swap test (CO-084); merge the rest into one canonical page (CO-083). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-043 — Invented author personas.** Banned: creating fictional writers — name, headshot, bio, credentials — to make the content program look staffed. Defeats: DET-CON-020. Bad: the plan launches "Meet our experts" with three generated portraits and invented job histories. Instead: credit real people with an author page and an independent trace, or use an honestly collective house byline (CO-086). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-044 — Expired claims left live by default.** Banned: letting dated copy (sale banners, "new for 2024", registration for past events) stay published past its date with no owner action. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Bad: the spring sale banner is still on the homepage in November because no page owned its expiry. Instead: every dated claim carries an owner and review-by date (CO-085) and is refreshed or retired on schedule (CO-089). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-041 — Brief traceability audit.** Verifies: CO-081, CO-087. Check: automated — diff the published URL inventory against the brief register; every published URL must map to a brief containing audience, goal, intent, owner, reviewer, and a cited evidence source. Pass: 100% of published URLs trace to a complete brief. Fail: unbriefed pages are pulled from the calendar owner's queue and briefed retroactively or unpublished. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-042 — Corpus similarity clustering.** Verifies: CO-083, CO-084, CO-090. Check: automated — cluster published pages by text similarity; for every cluster of more than three pages, apply the swap test to a sample pair. Pass: no cluster whose sampled pages are interchangeable after keyword swap. Fail: the set is merged to its canonical page or each page is rebuilt with verified page-specific data before the next release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-043 — Stale-date and review-by scan.** Verifies: CO-085, CO-089. Check: automated — extract date-bearing claims from published copy and diff the page inventory against the review-by register; flag any page past its review-by date and any claim asserting a past event as current. Pass: zero overdue pages and zero expired claims live. Fail: flagged pages are refreshed, retired, or re-dated with verification recorded before the next publish. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-044 — Authorship audit.** Verifies: CO-086. Check: manual — list every byline on the site; for each individual byline, require an author page plus one independent trace (staff page, professional profile); house bylines must name an accountable team, not a fake individual. Pass: every byline resolves to a real person or an honest collective. Fail: block publication under that byline until it does. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **The self-filling calendar.** An editorial calendar padded weeks ahead with topics nobody has briefed, so the schedule looks productive while every slot is an IOU. Catch it: pick any future slot at random — if no brief exists behind it, the calendar is decoration (CO-081).
- **Topic sprawl.** Chasing every adjacent query the keyword tool surfaces until the site publishes on subjects the business cannot serve or evidence. Catch it: for each new topic, ask "what do we operate, sell, or measure that makes us the source for this?" — no answer, no topic (CO-088).
- **Refresh theater.** Bumping a page's date, reordering paragraphs, and calling it a refresh while every claim stays unverified. Catch it: a refresh note that lists no claim re-checked against its source is a date edit, not a review (CO-089).
- **The deck-only strategy.** The plan lives in a slide deck that is never diffed against what actually shipped, so production quietly drifts into whatever was easiest to generate. Catch it: if the last brief traceability audit (G-CO-041) is older than the last publish, the strategy is not governing anything.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — The 200-city page matrix](examples/example-1.md) — corrects CO-084.
- [Example 2 — The article nobody briefed](examples/example-2.md) — corrects CO-081.
- [Example 3 — The evergreen page selling last spring's sale](examples/example-3.md) — corrects CO-085.

## Recall anchors

- No brief, no draft.
- Volume is an output, never a quota.
- One canonical page per topic; variants must survive the swap test.
- Every page: a real author, a named owner, a review-by date.
- Deepen the canonical page before spawning a sibling.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every item in production traces to a brief with audience, goal, intent, owner, and reviewer (G-CO-041).
- [ ] The plan states no pages-per-week or pages-per-month target anywhere (CO-082).
- [ ] Each topic maps to one canonical page; variants carry a written differentiation (CO-083).
- [ ] Every variant page passes the swap test with real page-specific data (CO-084).
- [ ] Every published page has a named owner and a review-by date (CO-085).
- [ ] All bylines are real people or an accountable house byline (G-CO-044).
- [ ] Each brief, refresh, and retirement cites the data behind it (CO-087).
- [ ] Similarity clustering shows no interchangeable page set (G-CO-042).

# copywriting

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies ; skills/detection/content/PARAMETERS.md (DET-CON-006, 007, 009, 010, 011, 017, 026, 027, 028)
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet, real-content
- **Feeds into:** on-page-seo, lifecycle-email, social-open-graph, structured-data

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Writing or editing any user-facing copy — landing pages, product pages, blog posts, metadata, alt text, captions, email and ad copy.
- **Do NOT use when:** The task is verifying whether a factual element may exist at all (that is real-content's gate; copywriting consumes its verdicts), setting topic inventory (content-strategy), or writing documentation (D10 owns documentation-writing; the voice guide is shared, not duplicated).

## Rules

1. **CO-101 — Competitor-verbatim test.** Every benefit sentence must name a mechanism, a user, or a verifiable outcome specific to this product. If a competitor could print the sentence unchanged, rewrite it with a product-specific fact from fact-sheet.md or delete it. (DET-CON-006)
2. **CO-102 — Fact-sheet traceability.** Every factual claim in copy — feature, number, price, name, outcome — traces to an entry in fact-sheet.md or a source record the business can produce. A claim with no trace is cut, never softened into vagueness.
3. **CO-103 — Cluster-term editing pass.** Before shipping, search the draft for model-default vocabulary clusters (delve, tapestry, realm, furthermore, moreover, "it's important to note", "in today's fast-paced world") and rewrite each hit in the house voice. Co-occurrence of several cluster terms on one page is a defect, not a style choice. (DET-CON-007)
4. **CO-104 — One qualifier maximum.** A product claim carries at most one honest qualifier. Three or more qualifiers stacked on one claim ("may potentially help to possibly improve") mean the claim is unverified: verify it and state it plainly, or cut it. (DET-CON-009)
5. **CO-105 — Measurable superlatives need substantiation.** "#1", "best-rated", "largest", and any rank, share, or rated-position claim require substantiation on file (ranking, survey, or criteria) before use; without it, rewrite as plain description. Unmeasurable puffery is a style note, not a finding. (DET-CON-026)
6. **CO-106 — No invented numbers.** Every statistic, percentage, rating, and count in copy cites its source or dataset, and one canonical figure is used site-wide. Third-party claims (ratings, market share, comparisons) need provenance somewhere on the domain; first-party counters need a fact-sheet entry. (DET-CON-011)
7. **CO-107 — No invented social proof.** Testimonials, review quotes, and endorsements are used only when a producible source record exists (signed quote, review-platform link, customer email) and permission is held. No record, no quote — the section ships empty or not at all. (DET-CON-010)
8. **CO-108 — Naming list is exact.** Company, product, feature, plan, and people names are copied from the project's naming list character-for-character — capitalization, spacing, and spelling — on every surface. Never re-type a name from memory. (DET-CON-017)
9. **CO-109 — Alt text from the rendered image.** Alt text and captions describe the actual rendered image: what a sighted reader sees. Never write them from the filename, a keyword list, or the prompt that generated the image. Decorative images get `alt=""`, not a description. (DET-CON-027)
10. **CO-110 — Structure follows the material.** Page structure — headings, paragraph order, length — varies with the subject. Never stamp one skeleton across pages with only keywords swapped; if two drafts share a heading sequence, rewrite one from its own brief. (DET-CON-008)
11. **CO-111 — Promises need backing.** A present-tense operational promise ("24/7 support", "money-back guarantee", "cancel anytime") appears in copy only when the policy page or documented process that makes it true exists and is linked. No backing artifact, no promise. (DET-CON-028)
12. **CO-112 — People-first, metadata last.** Copy is written to help the named reader complete a task, in the house voice guide's register; titles and descriptions are written after the page is finished, from what the page actually delivers. (Google people-first guidance)

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-051 — Invented testimonial.** Banned: a quoted endorsement from a person whose source record the business cannot produce. Defeats: DET-CON-010. Bad: "TaskBoard cut our planning time in half." — Sarah M., Marketing Manager (no such customer). Instead: use only a quote with a signed or platform-verifiable source record and permission, or ship the section without testimonials. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-052 — Unsourced statistic.** Banned: a precise figure (percentage, rating, user count, comparison) with no source, dataset, or fact-sheet entry behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Bad: "Teams ship 87% faster with TaskBoard." Instead: cite the dataset the figure came from and record it in fact-sheet.md, or delete the number and describe the mechanism. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-053 — Unsubstantiated measurable superlative.** Banned: a rank or rated-position claim ("#1", "best-rated", "the leading provider") with no ranking, survey, or criteria on file. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Bad: "The #1 project tool for remote teams." Instead: name the comparison set and source ("Top-rated in the 2026 Remote Work Tools survey, n=412"), or write a plain description of what the product does. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-054 — Competitor-verbatim benefit filler.** Banned: a benefit sentence any competitor could print unchanged, with no product-specific fact attached. Defeats: DET-CON-006. Bad: "Unlock the power of seamless collaboration and take your team to the next level." Instead: name the mechanism and outcome — "Comments resolve into tasks with one click, so decisions stop getting lost in threads." Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-CO-055 — Hedge stack.** Banned: three or more qualifiers protecting a single product claim. Defeats: DET-CON-009. Bad: "TaskBoard may potentially help your team to possibly improve how it might track work." Instead: verify and commit — "TaskBoard tracks every task's owner and due date in one board" — or cut the claim. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-051 — Pre-publish lint (automated).** Verifies: CO-103, CO-104. Check: run `grep -rniE "delve|tapestry|realm|furthermore|moreover|it's important to note|in today's fast-paced world" <copy files>` and a qualifier-cluster scan for `may|might|can` within five words of `potentially|possibly|generally`; every hit is listed for the editor. Pass: zero unrewritten hits. Fail: block shipment until the editor rewrites or justifies each hit in progress.md. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-052 — Substantiation spot-check (manual).** Verifies: CO-102, CO-105, CO-106, CO-107. Check: list every measurable claim, statistic, superlative, and testimonial in the piece; trace each to its fact-sheet entry or source record. Pass: 100% traced. Fail: block shipment; untraced items are cut, not footnoted. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-053 — Naming lint (automated).** Verifies: CO-108. Check: extract proper nouns from the copy and diff against the naming list; flag every variant form of a listed entity. Pass: exactly one live form per entity. Fail: block shipment until variants are corrected. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-054 — Competitor-verbatim review (manual).** Verifies: CO-101, CO-110. Check: highlight every benefit sentence and ask "could a competitor print this verbatim?"; on interior pages flag any yes with no specific within one sentence either side, on heroes judge the page as a whole; compare heading sequences against two sibling pages. Pass: no flagged sentence survives and no shared skeleton. Fail: warn and rewrite before publish. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Category-first drafting.** Opening a blank page and writing what "tools like this" say, then bolting the product name on. Catch it: if the draft was finished before fact-sheet.md was opened, restart from the fact sheet.
- **Synonym laundering.** Swapping generic words for fancier synonyms ("use" → "leverage" → "utilize") to fake specificity. Catch it: the sentence still names no mechanism after the swap — rewrite for fact, not vocabulary.
- **Padding instead of cutting.** When a page feels thin, adding paragraphs of altitude copy rather than one verified fact or a shorter page. Catch it: word count grew while the fact count stayed flat.
- **Register whiplash.** Hero in house voice, body in model-default register, because sections were drafted in separate sessions without the voice guide loaded. Catch it: read the page aloud end to end; a tone shift marks the unedited section.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Benefit filler rewritten with a mechanism](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects CO-101.
- [Example 2 — Hedge stack and cluster terms edited to a plain claim](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects CO-103, CO-104.
- [Example 3 — Superlative and statistic cut to substantiated copy](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects CO-105, CO-106.

## Recall anchors

- If a competitor could print it, rewrite it or cut it.
- No trace in the fact sheet, no claim on the page.
- Three qualifiers means unverified: commit or cut.
- Names are copied, never re-typed.
- Alt text describes the image you can see, not the file you named.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every benefit sentence passes the competitor-verbatim test (CO-101).
- [ ] Every factual claim traces to fact-sheet.md or a source record (CO-102).
- [ ] Cluster-term and hedge lint run; all hits rewritten (CO-103, CO-104, G-CO-051).
- [ ] Every superlative and statistic has substantiation on file (CO-105, CO-106, G-CO-052).
- [ ] Every testimonial has a producible source record and permission (CO-107).
- [ ] All names match the naming list exactly (CO-108, G-CO-053).
- [ ] Alt text and captions written from the rendered images (CO-109).
- [ ] Every operational promise links to its backing policy or process (CO-111).

# geo

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735 ; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features ; https://www.kevinleary.net/blog/llms-txt-myth/
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, on-page-seo, aeo, real-content, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** web-analytics, content-strategy

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** planning, executing, or reporting work aimed at inclusion and citation inside synthesized answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Google AI Overviews / AI Mode) — building citable content, aligning brand facts across sources, or measuring citation presence over time.
- **Do NOT use when:** the target is a ranked position, featured snippet, or AI Overview eligibility on Google Search itself (use aeo and technical-seo), when the deliverable is ordinary page copy (use copywriting), or when a claim's evidence is in dispute — resolve it under real-content first.

## Rules

1. **CO-061 — Every GEO claim carries an evidence tag.** Each tactic or claim in a GEO plan or report is labeled documented (platform-stated), peer-reviewed, correlational (vendor/observational), or hype (contradicted or unsupported); an untagged claim fails review.
2. **CO-062 — Documented layer first.** Before any GEO tactic is planned, the site meets Google's stated AI-features fundamentals: indexed and snippet-eligible, crawling allowed including at CDN/hosting level, important content in textual form and findable through internal links, structured data matching visible text.
3. **CO-063 — No special files, markup, or scores are requirements.** No plan presents llms.txt, a special schema type, a machine-readable AI file, or a paid "GEO score" as a platform requirement or platform metric — Google states none exist.
4. **CO-064 — llms.txt is hygiene, never a result.** llms.txt may be shipped as harmless hygiene; it is never reported as an AI-visibility win, because Google has stated on the record that it does not use the file and large-scale correlational evidence agrees.
5. **CO-065 — Citable content carries provenance.** Content built to be cited uses original data, named sources, direct quotations, and statistics with their source stated on the page — the methods the peer-reviewed GEO study measured; keyword stuffing is not a GEO method.
6. **CO-066 — Citability never overrides real content.** Every statistic, quotation, or credential added for citability passes real-content first: it traces to fact-sheet.md or a producible source record, or it is cut. An invented figure is a blocker even if an engine cites it.
7. **CO-067 — Brand facts are identical everywhere.** Name, offer, prices, and locations are word-for-word consistent across the site and major third-party profiles (business listings, directories, review platforms); engines synthesize across sources, so an off-site contradiction is treated as a site contradiction.
8. **CO-068 — One canonical statement per fact.** Each brand fact an engine might quote is stated once, canonically, on an owned page, and other pages link to or reuse that statement rather than re-typing a variant.
9. **CO-069 — Citation measurement uses a fixed prompt panel.** Measurement runs a fixed, written set of prompts per engine on a set cadence, with engine, model/version where shown, date, and cited sources logged per run; the panel changes only by a recorded decision.
10. **CO-070 — A single answer is an anecdote.** No report, dashboard, or client update presents one screenshot or one run as a citation result; reports show the panel, the number of runs, and the variance across runs.
11. **CO-071 — No guaranteed outcomes.** No plan, proposal, or report promises AI citation, inclusion, or a visibility percentage; peer-reviewed effects are quoted only with their limits (study's models, method, and "up to" bound), never as an expected average.
12. **CO-072 — Structured data matches visible text.** Any structured data on a page targeted for citation describes only what the page visibly shows, with identical values; markup describing absent content is removed, not "optimized".

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-031 — AI citation guarantee.** Banned: promising or implying guaranteed citation, inclusion, or a fixed visibility lift in AI answers. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Bad: proposal states "Our GEO package guarantees your brand appears in ChatGPT answers within 60 days." Instead: state the work and the measurement method, with each expected effect tagged by evidence level (CO-061, CO-071). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-032 — llms.txt reported as a visibility win.** Banned: listing llms.txt (or any special AI file/markup) in a results report as an AI-visibility achievement or requirement met. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; governed by CO-064. Bad: monthly report claims "AI readiness improved: llms.txt deployed, AI crawlers can now read the site." Instead: record llms.txt as hygiene in the change log only; report citation results from the prompt panel (CO-064, CO-069). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-033 — Invented statistic added for citability.** Banned: adding a statistic, quotation, or study result to content to make it more citable without a producible source behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Bad: a guide gains the line "Teams using checklists ship 43% faster (industry study)" with no study named or held. Instead: cite a named source on the page or use the project's own measured data from fact-sheet.md — otherwise cut the figure (CO-066). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-034 — Vendor metric presented as a platform fact.** Banned: presenting a vendor's GEO score, correlation study, or lift figure as a search/AI platform's stated ranking or citation factor. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Bad: plan states "Brand mentions are a confirmed AI ranking factor, so we will buy mention placements." Instead: label the study correlational, name its source, and treat it as a hypothesis the prompt panel can test (CO-061). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-CO-035 — Single-screenshot citation report.** Banned: reporting citation success or failure from one answer, one run, or one screenshot. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Bad: a slide shows one ChatGPT answer citing the brand, captioned "GEO is working — cited by ChatGPT." Instead: report the fixed prompt panel over repeated dated runs, including runs where the brand is absent (CO-069, CO-070). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-031 — Evidence-tag audit.** Verifies: CO-061, CO-071. Check: manual checklist over the GEO plan/report — every tactic and claim carries one of the four evidence tags, and every peer-reviewed figure is quoted with its limits. Pass: 100% tagged, no guarantees anywhere in the document. Fail: return the plan for tagging before any work starts. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-032 — Citation-claim provenance scan.** Verifies: CO-065, CO-066. Check: automated assist plus manual verdict — extract every statistic and attributed quotation from pages in the GEO set (`grep -rEo '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%' pages/ | sort -u`) and trace each to fact-sheet.md or a named on-page source. Pass: every figure traces; zero untraced figures. Fail: block shipment of the page. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-033 — Brand-fact consistency diff.** Verifies: CO-067, CO-068. Check: build the fact table (name, offer, prices, locations) from the site and each major third-party profile; diff every value against fact-sheet.md. Pass: zero conflicting values across all surfaces. Fail: correct the wrong surface before the measurement cycle starts. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-034 — Prompt-panel run log.** Verifies: CO-069, CO-070. Check: the citation tracker contains the fixed prompt set, one row per run with date, engine, and cited sources, and at least the scheduled number of runs for the period. Pass: log complete; reports cite panel aggregates only. Fail: mark the period's GEO results "insufficient data" — never substitute a single run. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Panel drift.** Prompts are quietly swapped after bad runs so the trend line improves; catch it by diffing the current panel against the version recorded when the cycle started.
- **Engine cherry-picking.** Results are reported only for the engine that cited the brand this month; catch it by requiring every report to show all engines in the panel, including zero-citation ones.
- **Citation bait clutter.** Pages accumulate tacked-on stat blocks and quote boxes that serve engines but confuse readers; catch it in editorial review — if a passage would be cut for a human reader, its citation value does not save it.
- **Fact fork.** A directory or profile keeps an old price or address because "engines read that one anyway"; catch it in the G-CO-033 diff — every surface is corrected, not just the website.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — GEO plan claims tagged by evidence level](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects CO-061, CO-071.
- [Example 2 — Statistic made citable with provenance, not invention](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects CO-065, CO-066.
- [Example 3 — Citation report rebuilt from a fixed prompt panel](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects CO-069, CO-070.

## Recall anchors

- No GEO claim without its evidence tag.
- Documented layer first: ordinary eligibility, accurate facts everywhere.
- llms.txt is hygiene — never report it as a result.
- Citable means sourced: an invented statistic is a blocker, cited or not.
- A single screenshot is an anecdote; the panel is the report.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every tactic and claim in the plan carries an evidence-level tag (CO-061, G-CO-031).
- [ ] Documented fundamentals verified: indexed, snippet-eligible, crawlable at CDN/hosting level, textual content, internal links (CO-062).
- [ ] No file, markup, or vendor score is presented as a platform requirement or metric (CO-063).
- [ ] Every statistic and quotation in GEO-targeted pages traces to fact-sheet.md or a named source (CO-066, G-CO-032).
- [ ] Brand facts diffed identical across the site and major third-party profiles (CO-067, G-CO-033).
- [ ] Citation results come from the fixed prompt panel over repeated dated runs — no single-run claims (CO-069, CO-070, G-CO-034).
- [ ] No guarantee of citation, inclusion, or visibility percentage appears anywhere in the deliverable (CO-071).

<!-- generated from skills/seo-content/growth-experiments/SKILL.md -->

# growth-experiments

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://docs.optimizely.com/experimentation-strategy/docs/take-action-based-on-the-results-of-an-experiment ; Kohavi, Tang & Xu, *Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments* (Cambridge University Press, 2020)
- **Depends on:** web-analytics, real-content
- **Feeds into:** content-strategy, copywriting

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an A/B test or controlled experiment on a page, flow, price display, or message is being planned, launched, read, or reported — and whenever an experiment result is cited in a decision, brief, or report.
- **Do NOT use when:** the change is a defect fix or a legal/compliance requirement (ship it; do not test whether to fix a bug), the question is what the data says without an intervention (use web-analytics), or the variant copy itself is being written (use copywriting — this skill governs the test around it).

## Rules

1. **CO-261 — Registered before launch.** Every experiment exists in the experiment register before it receives traffic, with: a hypothesis tied to a named user problem, exactly one primary metric, guardrail metrics, the surface it runs on, and an owner. An unregistered test does not launch.
2. **CO-262 — Sample size and runtime computed in advance.** Before launch, the register records the pre-computed sample size per variant, the expected traffic split, and a fixed end date covering at least one full business cycle for the surface (a full week minimum on weekly-cycle traffic). "Run it until it looks significant" is not a runtime.
3. **CO-263 — No peeking decisions.** Results are read at the pre-registered horizon. The only exception is a sequential-testing method (e.g. an alpha-spending or always-valid p-value approach) named in the register before launch. A test stopped early because a variant was "winning" is void and is recorded as void.
4. **CO-264 — The primary metric decides.** The ship / kill / extend decision follows the primary metric alone. Secondary metrics may generate the next hypothesis; they never overturn, soften, or substitute for the primary result.
5. **CO-265 — One experiment per surface.** Two experiments never run on the same surface at the same time unless the register records an interaction-aware design (mutually exclusive buckets or a factorial design) before either launches.
6. **CO-266 — Random assignment, verified split.** Traffic is assigned randomly at the pre-registered split, and a sample ratio mismatch (SRM) check runs before any result is read. An SRM failure invalidates the experiment: the result is not interpreted, the assignment bug is fixed, and the test restarts.
7. **CO-267 — Effect size with a confidence interval.** Every reported result states the primary-metric effect size and its confidence interval, the sample sizes, and the runtime. A bare "significant" / "not significant" verdict, or a percentage lift with no interval, is not a reportable result.
8. **CO-268 — Variants pass the real-content gates.** Variant copy and claims pass the same gates as any shipped page before launch: no fabricated claim or statistic, no unsubstantiated superlative (DET-CON-026), no promise without a backing process (DET-CON-028). An experiment never tests whether a false claim converts better.
9. **CO-269 — Every conclusion is recorded, including losers.** At the horizon, the register entry is completed with the SRM result, the primary-metric effect and interval, and the decision (ship, kill, or inconclusive-extend with its reason). Losing and inconclusive experiments are recorded with the same completeness as winners; an experiment with no completed entry is treated as never having run.
10. **CO-270 — Guardrails can veto a win.** If a guardrail metric (e.g. revenue per visitor, unsubscribe rate, page performance, error rate) degrades beyond the bound set in the register, the variant does not ship even when the primary metric improves; the conflict is recorded in the entry.
11. **CO-271 — No mid-flight changes.** Variant content, traffic split, primary metric, and end date do not change after launch. A needed change closes the experiment as inconclusive and restarts it under a new register ID with the change recorded.
12. **CO-272 — Reports trace to the register.** Any number quoted from an experiment — in a report, brief, case study, or page — matches the register entry and its underlying results export exactly. Screenshots of a dashboard mid-flight and recollected figures are not sources.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-131 — The peek-and-stop win.** Banned: ending an experiment before its pre-registered horizon because an interim look showed a variant ahead, and reporting that lead as a result. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Bad: on day two the dashboard shows variant B up 18% at p = 0.04; the test is stopped and the weekly report announces "B wins, +18% conversions". Instead: run to the registered horizon (or use a sequential method named in advance, CO-263) and report the effect with its confidence interval. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-132 — The secondary-metric rescue.** Banned: declaring success on a secondary metric after the primary metric came back flat or negative. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Bad: signup rate (primary) is unchanged, but time-on-page rose, so the experiment is reported as a win and the variant ships. Instead: record the decision the primary metric dictates (CO-264); log the secondary observation as the hypothesis for a new registered experiment. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-133 — Testing a fabricated claim.** Banned: putting an invented statistic, testimonial, or unsubstantiated superlative into a variant to see if it lifts conversion. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Bad: variant B's headline reads "Join 50,000+ teams — rated #1 by founders", figures the business cannot produce a source for. Instead: variants use only fact-sheet-backed claims (CO-268); test the presentation of a true claim, never the invention of one. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-134 — The unrecorded experiment.** Banned: running, stopping, or citing an experiment that has no register entry, or quoting its outcome from memory or a dashboard screenshot. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Bad: "We tested the red button last month, it did about 10% better" appears in a planning brief, with no hypothesis, sample size, or data anywhere. Instead: no entry, no experiment (CO-261); results are cited only from a completed register entry and its export (CO-272). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-135 — The unbacked-promise variant.** Banned: testing a variant whose offer, guarantee, or service promise has no backing policy or process behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Bad: variant B promises "replies within one hour, guaranteed" on a support page staffed for next-business-day responses. Instead: the promise ships in a variant only when the process that makes it true exists and is linked (CO-268). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-131 — SRM check (automated).** Verifies: CO-266. Check: in the results pipeline, run the chi-square test on observed vs expected assignment counts, e.g. `python3 -c "from scipy.stats import chisquare; print(chisquare([5231, 4769], f_exp=[5000, 5000]))"` with the experiment's real counts substituted. Pass: p-value > 0.001. Fail: the result is void — do not read the metrics; fix the assignment, record the failure, restart. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-132 — Pre-launch registration check.** Verifies: CO-261, CO-262, CO-265. Check: `grep -A 12 "EXP-<id>" experiments/register.md` and confirm the entry shows the hypothesis, one primary metric, guardrails, pre-computed sample size, fixed end date, surface, and owner — and that no other active entry names the same surface. Pass: all fields present, surface exclusive. Fail: block the launch until the entry is complete. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-133 — Variant real-content pass.** Verifies: CO-268. Check: extract every claim, figure, and promise from each variant and trace it to fact-sheet.md or a producible source record; assist with `grep -niE "best|#1|guarantee|risk-free|trusted by|% (faster|better|more)" variants/<id>/` and clear or cut each hit. Pass: every claim traced. Fail: the variant does not launch. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-134 — Horizon and decision audit.** Verifies: CO-263, CO-264, CO-269. Check: manual audit of the last concluded experiment — the decision date is on or after the registered end date, the recorded decision follows the primary metric, and the entry carries the SRM result, effect size, and confidence interval. Pass: all four hold. Fail: the conclusion is withdrawn, the entry corrected, and the result is not cited anywhere until it passes. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CO-135 — Register completeness sweep.** Verifies: CO-269, CO-272. Check: list every experiment marked concluded in the register; each has a completed entry (hypothesis, primary metric, SRM, effect, decision), including losers and inconclusive runs. Pass: zero concluded experiments with incomplete entries. Fail: complete the entries from the results exports before any new launch. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **The daily dashboard glance.** Checking the experiment every day "just to watch", then unconsciously timing unrelated decisions around a mid-flight lead. Catch it: if you cannot state the pre-registered end date without looking it up, you are watching, not running a test.
- **The kitchen-sink variant.** Variant B changes the headline, price display, layout, and CTA at once, so a win (or loss) can never be attributed. Catch it: a variant that needs the word "and" twice to describe what changed is several experiments pretending to be one.
- **Novelty read as durability.** A week-one spike from returning users reacting to any visible change is reported as a lasting lift. Catch it: results read before one full business cycle, or with no new-vs-returning split considered, get an inconclusive-extend, not a ship.
- **The underpowered null.** Traffic far below the pre-computed sample size produces "no significant difference", which is then quoted as proof the change does not matter. Catch it: compare achieved sample against the CO-262 computation — an underpowered null is an inconclusive result, recorded as such.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — The two-day "winner"](examples/example-1.md) — corrects CO-263 and CO-266.
- [Example 2 — The secondary-metric rescue](examples/example-2.md) — corrects CO-264 and CO-269.
- [Example 3 — The variant with an unbacked promise](examples/example-3.md) — corrects CO-268.

## Recall anchors

- Registered before launch, or it does not run.
- Read at the horizon, never at the peek.
- The primary metric decides; secondaries only suggest the next test.
- SRM first — a broken split voids everything downstream.
- Losers get register entries too.

## Checklist

- [ ] Register entry complete before launch: hypothesis, one primary metric, guardrails, owner (G-CO-132).
- [ ] Sample size computed and end date fixed, covering at least one full business cycle (CO-262).
- [ ] Surface is exclusive to this experiment, or an interaction-aware design is recorded (CO-265).
- [ ] Every variant claim traced to the fact sheet — no invented figures, superlatives, or unbacked promises (G-CO-133).
- [ ] SRM check passed before any metric was read (G-CO-131).
- [ ] Decision taken at the horizon, on the primary metric, with guardrails checked (CO-263, CO-264, CO-270).
- [ ] Register entry completed with effect size, confidence interval, SRM result, and decision — win, loss, or inconclusive (G-CO-135).
