<!-- generated from skills/cloning-replication/fidelity-verification/SKILL.md -->

# fidelity-verification

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D16 Cloning & Replication (CL)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots ; http://umatechnology.org/best-seo-site-migration-monitoring-tools-for-redirects-crawling-and-indexing/
- **Depends on:** clone-ethics (D14 gate), page-inventory, design-extraction, behavior-cloning, page-reconstruction
- **Feeds into:** handover

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** An authorized rebuild is ready to be proven against its source — per inventory page, at the agreed viewports, with pixel diffing, DOM comparison, and the behavior-cloning interaction checklist.
- **Do NOT use when:** No D14 authorization record or frozen capture set exists (stop; site-discovery and clone-ethics come first), when a page is labeled `designed` in page-reconstruction (it carries no parity claim to verify), or as a substitute for D8 functional QA on the rebuild's own features.

## Rules

1. **CL-121 — Verify against the frozen capture set.** All comparisons run against the authorized WARC/CDX captures frozen at inventory sign-off, never against the live source, so the target cannot drift mid-verification.
2. **CL-122 — Fix viewports and thresholds before the first run.** The viewport list, the similarity bar (≥95% pixel similarity on key viewports), the per-page vs. aggregate scoring rule, and the masking rules are committed in writing before any comparison runs.
3. **CL-123 — Same engine, same conditions.** Source captures and rebuild screenshots are produced in the same browser engine and version, at the same viewport, in the same state (auth state, fixture data, locale); a mismatch in conditions invalidates the run.
4. **CL-124 — Verify page by page against the inventory.** Every in-scope inventory row receives a comparison result; a page with no run is reported as unverified, never silently counted as passing.
5. **CL-125 — Mask dynamic regions by rule.** Timestamps, rotating content, and similar dynamic regions are masked only via selectors/rules committed under CL-122 before the run; no region is masked ad hoc to rescue a failing page.
6. **CL-126 — Compare DOM structure alongside pixels.** Each comparison reports a structural diff (headings, landmarks, interactive elements present/absent) next to the pixel score; a pixel pass with missing structure is a defect.
7. **CL-127 — Run the behavior checklist per element.** The interaction tests recorded by behavior-cloning execute against the rebuild for every in-scope interactive element; verification is incomplete while any in-scope element is untested.
8. **CL-128 — Log every difference.** Each above-tolerance diff becomes a defect entry or an accepted-deviation record naming the page, the difference, the reason, and the approver; differences are never absorbed into a prose summary.
9. **CL-129 — Baseline changes need a reason and re-approval.** A golden baseline is regenerated only with a recorded reason tied to an approved change; the change and its approver are logged before the new baseline is committed.
10. **CL-130 — Score font deltas by the substitution record.** Where design-extraction recorded a licensed-font substitution, the expected rendering delta is scored as that accepted deviation; it is never hidden by widening a mask or the tolerance.
11. **CL-131 — Exclude and report unverifiable views.** A source view that cannot be captured within the D14 authorization and robots rules is excluded from scoring and listed as unverified in the report; it is never captured by bypass and never scored by guess.
12. **CL-132 — Every claim cites its run.** Any fidelity statement in a deliverable (a percentage, "verified", a per-page verdict) names the run that produced it: date, engine, viewport set, and per-page scores.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CL-061 — Eyeball verdict.** Banned: declaring a page "pixel-perfect", "identical", or "verified" from looking at two screenshots with no diff run behind the claim. Defeats: DET-CRWL-002. Bad: the report says the pricing page is "a pixel-perfect clone" after a side-by-side glance. Instead: run the committed visual comparison and cite its per-page score and diff image. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-062 — Silent baseline regeneration.** Banned: regenerating a golden baseline so a failing comparison turns green, with no reason record. Defeats: DET-CRWL-018. Bad: the home page diff fails at 91%, the baseline is re-screenshotted from the rebuild, and the suite passes at 100%. Instead: log the difference as a defect or an accepted deviation under CL-128, and regenerate only under CL-129. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-063 — Post-failure renegotiation.** Banned: lowering the similarity bar, dropping a viewport, or switching from per-page to aggregate scoring after a run has failed. Defeats: DET-CRWL-018. Bad: after two pages score 93%, the bar is "revisited" to 90% so the report can ship. Instead: keep the CL-122 thresholds; fix the pages or record accepted deviations with reasons. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-064 — Bypass capture for scoring.** Banned: defeating a login, paywall, or robots rule to screenshot a source view for the comparison. Defeats: DET-CRWL-008. Bad: a borrowed customer login is used to capture the dashboard so it can be scored. Instead: exclude the view under CL-131 and report it as unverified, or capture it only through access the client legitimately provisions. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-065 — Full-size source assets in reports.** Banned: embedding the target's full-resolution photography, artwork, or trademark assets in comparison reports beyond the thumbnails the diff itself requires. Defeats: DET-CRWL-009. Bad: the verification appendix ships the source's full-size hero images and logo files "for reference." Instead: include only the expected/actual/diff thumbnails the comparison generated, and reference source assets by capture ID. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CL-061 — Visual comparison suite (automated).** Verifies: CL-122, CL-124. Check: run the Playwright visual comparison suite in CI against the committed baselines (`npx playwright test --grep @visual`) and collect the per-page diff report. Pass: every in-scope page has a result and every key viewport scores ≥95% similarity or carries an accepted-deviation record. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: NOT APPLICABLE — no source captures exist to baseline against and this mode makes no visual-parity claim; visual quality is gated by G-CL-025 (adapted) and the D13 gates; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-062 — Baseline-change audit (automated).** Verifies: CL-129. Check: script lists baseline files changed since the last approved run (`git diff --name-only <last-approved-tag> -- tests/visual/baselines/`) and asserts each has a matching reason record in the deviation log. Pass: zero baseline changes without a reason record and approver. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: NOT APPLICABLE — no baselines exist (follows G-CL-061); rebuild regression-baseline changes are reviewed under G-CL-064 (adapted); see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-063 — Interaction checklist completeness (automated).** Verifies: CL-127. Check: diff the behavior-cloning in-scope element/flow list against the executed checklist results; any element with no passing test result is listed. Pass: zero untested in-scope elements. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CL-064 — Deviation log review (manual).** Verifies: CL-128, CL-131. Check: review the defect/deviation log against the latest diff report; every above-tolerance diff has a defect entry or an accepted deviation with reason and approver, and every unverified page is listed with its exclusion reason. Pass: log accounts for 100% of reported differences. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — the review runs over the deviation log against the playbook's disposition table; every adapted or not-applicable gate and excluded row must carry its entry and reason; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-065 — Report claim check (automated).** Verifies: CL-132. Check: `grep -rniE 'pixel-perfect|[0-9]+% similar|verified clone' deliverables/` and assert each match cites a run ID present in the verification results store. Pass: no fidelity claim without a backing run. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Aggregate-only reporting.** A single "97% overall" hides the two pages at 88%. Catch it: require the per-page minimum next to any aggregate figure before accepting a report.
- **Viewport cherry-picking.** Only the desktop viewport is compared because mobile "is responsive anyway." Catch it: diff the run's viewport list against the CL-122 committed set.
- **Mask creep.** Masked regions grow run over run until half a page is excluded from scoring. Catch it: track masked-area percentage per page across runs and question any increase.
- **Stale-condition comparison.** The rebuild is screenshotted logged-in while the source capture is logged-out, and the "differences" are all session chrome. Catch it: check the run manifest's state fields against CL-123 before reading scores.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Eyeball verdict vs. measured diff run](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects CL-124, BAN-CL-061.
- [Example 2 — Regenerated baseline vs. reason-recorded change](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects CL-129, BAN-CL-062.
- [Example 3 — Buried failing page vs. per-page deviation log](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects CL-128, CL-131.

## Recall anchors

- No run, no verdict — fidelity is measured, never eyeballed.
- Thresholds and viewports are fixed before the first run, not after a failure.
- Baselines are evidence: regenerate only with a reason and re-approval.
- Every difference is a defect or an accepted deviation with a name on it.
- Unverifiable means excluded and reported — never bypassed, never guessed.

## Checklist

- [ ] Viewport list, ≥95% bar, scoring rule, and masking rules committed before the first run (CL-122).
- [ ] Comparisons ran against the frozen capture set in one engine under matched conditions (CL-121, CL-123).
- [ ] Every in-scope inventory page has a comparison result or an unverified listing (CL-124, CL-131).
- [ ] DOM structure diff reported alongside every pixel score (CL-126).
- [ ] Interaction checklist shows zero untested in-scope elements (G-CL-063).
- [ ] Every above-tolerance diff is a defect or an accepted deviation with reason and approver (CL-128).
- [ ] Baseline-change audit passes: no unexplained baseline changes (G-CL-062).
- [ ] Every fidelity claim in the deliverables cites its run (CL-132, G-CL-065).

<!-- generated from skills/cloning-replication/page-inventory/SKILL.md -->

# page-inventory

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D16 Cloning & Replication (CL)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Wayback CDX Server API — https://github.com/internetarchive/wayback/blob/master/wayback-cdx-server/README.md ; migration inventory practice (crawl + sitemap + analytics + Search Console merge) — https://guestpost.uk/screaming-frog/
- **Depends on:** site-discovery, clone-ethics
- **Feeds into:** design-extraction, asset-harvesting, behavior-cloning, page-reconstruction, fidelity-verification

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an authorized discovery crawl exists and the replication scope must be fixed as one reconciled table — the contract every later D16 skill builds, samples, and verifies against.
- **Do NOT use when:** discovery has not run (use site-discovery first), the D14 authorization record does not exist (stop; clone-ethics gates all D16 work), or the deliverable is a content copy — the inventory is a map of pages, never a harvest of the target's text or imagery.

## Rules

1. **CL-021 — Four-source merge.** The inventory is built by merging the rendered crawl, the XML sitemap(s), analytics/Search Console top pages, and the Wayback CDX index. If client analytics access is unavailable, the three remaining sources are the minimum and the missing source is recorded on the inventory header — never silently skipped.
2. **CL-022 — One row per canonical page.** Each row is one canonical URL after normalization (trailing slash, query parameters, casing resolved; redirect sources resolved to their target). A redirect source is an attribute of its target row, never a row itself.
3. **CL-023 — Mandatory row fields.** Every row carries: canonical URL, page type, template ID, component set, HTTP status, last capture date, provenance flag (`public`, `archived-only`, or `inferred`), scope status (`built`, `planned`, or `excluded`), and priority. A row missing any field is unfinished, not filed.
4. **CL-024 — Templates by DOM structure.** Rows are clustered into template families by DOM structure, so shared layouts are built once. Pages differing only in data (product, post, profile) share one parameterized template row set; a template ID is assigned before any reconstruction starts.
5. **CL-025 — States and viewports are rows too.** Materially distinct states (logged-out vs. logged-in shell, empty vs. populated list, error state) and viewport variants that change layout are inventoried as variant rows linked to their parent page, with their own priority.
6. **CL-026 — No silent deletion.** A discovered page that is out of scope stays in the table with scope status `excluded` and a one-line reason. "Missing" and "excluded" must always be distinguishable; a row is removed only by merging it as a duplicate, with the merge recorded.
7. **CL-027 — Count reconciliation.** The inventory row count equals the reconciled discovery count from site-discovery. Every URL present in one source and absent from another carries a reconciliation note (orphan, sitemap-only, archived-only, JS-route) before sign-off.
8. **CL-028 — Signed scope contract.** The client signs off the in-scope count (`built` + `planned` rows) before reconstruction starts. That count is the engagement's scope contract; pages discovered later enter through a recorded scope change, not by quiet addition.
9. **CL-029 — Authorized input only.** The inventory is built only from authorized discovery output and inherits its robots.txt compliance. It is never extended by fetching disallowed paths; gated pages are listed as gated with provenance noted, never accessed by bypass.
10. **CL-030 — Map, not copy.** Rows record provenance and rights-relevant facts (for example, pages whose assets are third-party) but never embed the target's copyrighted text, imagery, or branded assets as reusable content.
11. **CL-031 — Evidence frozen at sign-off.** At scope sign-off the underlying evidence set (captures, crawl output, CDX responses) is frozen and referenced by the inventory version, so later skills verify against the same baseline even if the live site changes.
12. **CL-032 — Versioned table.** The inventory is a committed, versioned file. Every change after sign-off (new row, status change, template re-cluster) is a dated revision entry, so any later fidelity result can be traced to the inventory version it was checked against.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CL-011 — Navigation-only inventory.** Banned: building the inventory from the site's navigation menu or homepage links alone and presenting it as all pages. Defeats: DET-CRWL-007. Bad: the inventory lists the 14 menu pages of a store while 300 product and blog pages from the sitemap and CDX index never appear. Instead: merge crawl, sitemap, analytics, and CDX sources and reconcile the differences (CL-021, CL-027). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-012 — Silent row deletion.** Banned: deleting out-of-scope or inconvenient rows so the table looks complete. Defeats: DET-CRWL-005. Bad: 40 archived-only landing pages are dropped from the draft, and the final report claims the inventory covers "the whole site." Instead: keep every discovered row with scope status `excluded` and a stated reason (CL-026). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-013 — Duplicate canonical rows.** Banned: listing the same page more than once under URL variants (trailing slash, tracking parameters, casing, redirect source). Defeats: DET-CRWL-005. Bad: `/pricing`, `/pricing/`, and `/pricing?utm_source=ad` appear as three rows and are rebuilt as three pages. Instead: canonicalize and merge into one row, with variants recorded as attributes (CL-022). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-014 — Extending the inventory by disallowed fetching.** Banned: fetching robots-disallowed, login-gated, or paywalled URLs to "complete" the inventory. Defeats: DET-CRWL-014. Bad: the crawler logs in with a borrowed account to enumerate the dashboard pages the public crawl cannot see. Instead: list gated pages as gated from authorized evidence only, and record disallowed paths as excluded by robots (CL-029). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-015 — Inventory as content copy.** Banned: pasting the target's page copy, headlines, or image files into inventory rows as reusable content. Defeats: DET-CRWL-009. Bad: each row carries the target's full marketing text "so reconstruction can paste it back." Instead: rows carry URLs, structure, and rights facts only; content is recreated or replaced downstream (CL-030). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CL-011 — Reconciliation diff.** Verifies: CL-021, CL-027. Check: automated — script compares the inventory's canonical URL set against the reconciled site-discovery URL set (crawl ∪ sitemap ∪ analytics ∪ CDX); any URL in one set and not the other, without a reconciliation note, fails. Pass: zero unexplained differences. Fail: block scope sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — the reconciled set is the pattern inventory's route set, not the crawl/sitemap/analytics/CDX union; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-012 — Classification completeness.** Verifies: CL-023, CL-026. Check: automated — script asserts every row has all mandatory fields populated and a scope status of `built`, `planned`, or `excluded`, and that every `excluded` row carries a non-empty reason. Pass: 100% of rows fully classified. Fail: block scope sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CL-013 — Canonical uniqueness.** Verifies: CL-022. Check: automated — canonicalize every row URL (lowercase host, resolve trailing slash and tracking parameters, follow recorded redirects to target) and assert the resulting set has no duplicates. Pass: zero duplicate canonical URLs. Fail: block scope sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CL-014 — Robots and gating audit.** Verifies: CL-029. Check: automated — compare the inventory's source URLs against the discovery crawl's robots.txt Disallow set and gated-path list; any row whose evidence came from a disallowed fetch or a bypassed gate fails. Pass: zero violations. Fail: block the engagement pending D14 review. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — the audit asserts pattern-reference provenance on every row and zero fetches in the crawl log; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-015 — Sample verification.** Verifies: CL-023, CL-024. Check: manual — fetch a random 10% sample of rows and confirm URL, HTTP status, and template label against the live page or its archived capture. Pass: every sampled row matches; any mismatch triggers a full re-check of its template family. Fail: block scope sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: NOT APPLICABLE — no live page or archived capture may be consulted; row accuracy is covered by G-CL-011 (adapted) and G-CL-012; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.

## Anti-patterns

- **Round-number scope.** The inventory lands on a suspiciously round count ("exactly 100 pages") because discovery stopped at a crawl limit. Catch it: compare the count against each source's raw total; a cap hit during any source pull invalidates the merge until re-run uncapped.
- **Template inflation.** Near-identical pages are each given their own template ID, so reconstruction rebuilds one layout twenty times. Catch it: sort rows by DOM-structure hash; families differing only in text or data merge into one parameterized template (CL-024).
- **Priority by menu order.** Priorities simply mirror the navigation order instead of traffic and business value. Catch it: cross-check priority against the analytics top-pages source; a high-traffic page ranked below a footer link means priority was guessed.
- **Stale-status drift.** Rows keep the HTTP status and capture date from the first crawl while the site changes underneath. Catch it: any row whose last capture date predates the evidence freeze (CL-031) without a re-check note is flagged before sign-off.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Four sources merged, one reconciled table](examples/example-1.md) — corrects CL-021.
- [Example 2 — URL variants merged into one canonical row](examples/example-2.md) — corrects CL-022.
- [Example 3 — Out-of-scope pages kept as excluded rows](examples/example-3.md) — corrects CL-026.

## Recall anchors

- The inventory is the contract: if it is not a row, it is out of scope — in writing.
- Four sources in, one canonical row per page.
- Excluded is a status with a reason, never a deletion.
- Gated pages are listed as gated, never fetched around.
- Sign-off freezes the count and the evidence.

## Checklist

- [ ] All four sources merged, or the missing source recorded on the header (CL-021).
- [ ] Canonical URLs unique across rows; redirect sources are attributes, not rows (G-CL-013).
- [ ] Every row fully classified: built, planned, or excluded with a reason (G-CL-012).
- [ ] Row count reconciles with site-discovery, differences noted (G-CL-011).
- [ ] No row's evidence came from a disallowed or bypassed fetch (G-CL-014).
- [ ] States and viewport variants inventoried as linked variant rows (CL-025).
- [ ] Client signed off the in-scope count; evidence set frozen and versioned (CL-028, CL-031).

<!-- generated from skills/cloning-replication/page-reconstruction/SKILL.md -->

# page-reconstruction

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D16 Cloning & Replication (CL)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://github.com/internetarchive/wayback/blob/master/wayback-cdx-server/README.md ; https://www.w3.org/community/reports/design-tokens/CG-FINAL-format-20251028/
- **Depends on:** page-inventory, design-extraction, clone-ethics (D14)
- **Feeds into:** fidelity-verification

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an in-scope inventory page cannot be captured directly — it is auth-gated, deleted, or never archived — and must be rebuilt from surviving evidence.
- **Do NOT use when:** the page was captured intact; build from the capture instead. Do NOT use when no D14 authorization record covers reconstruction; stop and route to clone-ethics first.

## Rules

1. **CL-101 — Authorization precedes reconstruction.** No page is reconstructed before the D14 authorization record exists and names reconstruction in scope; the record's date is checked against the first build artifact's date.
2. **CL-102 — Evidence hierarchy is binding.** Rebuild from the highest available tier: (1) dated Wayback captures, (2) JS bundle route manifests, sitemap hints, and API responses, (3) the extracted design system and component patterns. A lower tier is used only after the tiers above it are checked and recorded as absent.
3. **CL-103 — Every row carries a status.** Each inventory row is labeled `captured`, `inferred`, or `designed` before its build starts; the label is stored in the inventory, not in the builder's head.
4. **CL-104 — Parity claims attach to `captured` only.** Only a `captured` page may be described as a clone or as matching the source. An `inferred` page is "reconstructed from partial evidence"; a `designed` page is "new design in the source's system."
5. **CL-105 — Build follows inventory order.** Pages are built in the priority order fixed in the page inventory; nothing outside the inventory is improvised, however plausible it seems.
6. **CL-106 — Operator content only.** Reconstructed pages render with the operator's own copy, data, and branding. Recovered target copy is a structural reference (length, placement, hierarchy) and is replaced unless the client owns the rights, per the D14 record.
7. **CL-107 — No target assets ship.** The target's images, logos, wordmarks, and trade dress never appear in a reconstructed page; placeholders or operator assets stand in, and each substitution is listed in the build notes.
8. **CL-108 — Structure from evidence, code original.** Layout and function are recreated from the evidence and the design-token file; markup and code are written fresh for the rebuild, never lifted from the target's served source.
9. **CL-109 — Gated pages need provided access.** An auth-gated page is reconstructed only from client-provided access or client-provided evidence (exports, screenshots, recordings). Absence from archives is never a reason to bypass the gate.
10. **CL-110 — Capture claims verified by digest.** A Wayback capture is cited as evidence only after its CDX `digest` and timestamp are recorded in the inventory row, so what the capture actually contained is checkable later.
11. **CL-111 — Inferred structure is spot-verified.** Every route or component inferred from a bundle manifest or API response is cross-checked against at least one second evidence item (sitemap entry, capture fragment, or client confirmation) before build.
12. **CL-112 — Deviations are logged, not hidden.** Where evidence runs out mid-page, the gap and the design decision that filled it are written into the inventory row's notes before the page is marked built.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CL-051 — Fabricated page labeled a verified clone.** Banned: inventing a plausible page from generic patterns and calling it a clone of a page nobody has seen. Defeats: DET-CRWL-013. Bad: a dashboard assembled from a UI kit is delivered as "verified clone of the admin console," a page that was never captured. Instead: label the row `designed`, build it in the source's design system, and present it to the client as new design. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-052 — Target copy and branding shipped verbatim.** Banned: resurrecting the target's text, photography, logo, or trade dress in the reconstructed page. Defeats: DET-CRWL-009. Bad: headlines and hero photography recovered from a capture are pasted into the rebuild unchanged. Instead: use recovered material as a structural reference only and replace it with the operator's own content unless the D14 record confirms the client owns the rights. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-053 — Bypassing a gate to obtain evidence.** Banned: using borrowed credentials, a shared login, or a paywall workaround to see a page that archives do not hold. Defeats: DET-CRWL-008. Bad: the builder logs in with a customer's credentials found in a forum post to screenshot a members-only page. Instead: record the page as gated and reconstruct only from client-provided access or evidence. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-054 — Skipping a higher evidence tier.** Banned: reconstructing from the design system or from memory while an unchecked Wayback capture or bundle manifest exists. Defeats: DET-CRWL-002. Bad: a deleted pricing page is rebuilt from a screenshot in a blog post although three dated CDX captures were never queried. Instead: query and record every higher tier first; only a recorded absence licenses the next tier down. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-055 — Improvising pages outside the inventory.** Banned: adding pages, sections, or flows that appear in no inventory row because they "must have existed." Defeats: DET-CRWL-013. Bad: a settings page is invented to complete a navigation menu that has a gap. Instead: build only inventory rows; raise the gap as an inventory question for the client. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CL-051 — Inventory status audit (automated).** Verifies: CL-103. Check: script scans the inventory table and fails on any row whose status field is empty or outside {`captured`, `inferred`, `designed`}. Pass: 100% of rows carry a valid status. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CL-052 — Parity-claim check (automated).** Verifies: CL-104. Check: grep deliverable docs, page metadata, and filenames for parity-claim phrases — "identical to", "1:1", "pixel-perfect", "exact copy of", "matches the original", "verified copy", "same as" followed by the target's name — joined to any row not labeled `captured`; any match fails. Matching is by claim phrase, never by the bare word "clone": the word clone in a project name (e.g. ShopClone), a file name, or a reference to this playbook or skill family is not a parity claim and is never flagged. Pass: zero matches. Fail: block shipment until the claim is corrected. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-CL-053 — Template-coverage and content check (automated).** Verifies: CL-105, CL-106, CL-107. Check: script asserts every inventory row maps to exactly one built template, renders each template with the operator's content set, and greps the rendered output and asset folders for the target's domain, logo filenames, and recovered copy strings; any hit fails. Pass: full coverage, zero target strings or assets. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — coverage runs unchanged, and the target-string grep compares against the pattern inventory's protected-items list; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-054 — Evidence-tier log review.** Verifies: CL-102, CL-110, CL-111. Check: manual review of each `inferred`/`designed` row's notes — a CDX digest + timestamp for capture-based claims, a recorded absence for each skipped tier, and a second evidence item for each inferred route. Pass: every row's evidence chain is complete. Fail: return the row to evidence gathering. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — the evidence chain is the pattern-inventory citation, the zero-fetch crawl log as the recorded absence of capture tiers, and the design record; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-055 — Authorization pre-flight.** Verifies: CL-101, CL-109. Check: confirm the D14 authorization record exists, predates the first reconstruction artifact, and names reconstruction in scope; list every gated row and its client-provided evidence source. Pass: record valid and every gated row sourced legitimately. Fail: block all reconstruction work. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Screenshot-memory drift.** The builder "remembers" roughly how the page looked and fills gaps from that impression; catch it by requiring every layout claim to point at a capture, manifest line, or token before it is built.
- **Uniform-confidence reporting.** The progress summary lists all pages as "rebuilt" with no status split, so the client cannot tell evidence from invention; catch it by reporting counts per status label in every update.
- **Gap-filling by symmetry.** A missing page variant is mirrored from its sibling (the "cancel" flow copied from "confirm") without evidence it existed; catch it by checking each variant against its own inventory row.
- **Polish before provenance.** Effort goes into making an inferred page look finished before its evidence chain is recorded, and the polish quietly becomes the claim; catch it by running G-CL-054 before any visual pass.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — The deleted pricing page](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects CL-102, CL-110.
- [Example 2 — The gated admin console](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects CL-104, CL-109.
- [Example 3 — Recovered copy in the rebuild](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects CL-106, CL-107.

## Recall anchors

- Highest evidence tier first; a skipped tier needs a recorded absence.
- Only `captured` pages may claim parity — everything else is labeled honestly.
- Structure from the target, content from the operator.
- No inventory row, no page.
- A gate is a fact about access, never an obstacle to route around.

## Checklist

- [ ] D14 authorization record exists, predates the build, and names reconstruction (CL-101).
- [ ] Every inventory row labeled `captured`, `inferred`, or `designed` (CL-103).
- [ ] CDX digest and timestamp recorded for every capture used as evidence (CL-110).
- [ ] Higher tiers recorded as absent before any lower tier was used (CL-102).
- [ ] No parity language attached to `inferred` or `designed` rows (CL-104, G-CL-052).
- [ ] Rendered pages contain only operator copy, data, and branding (CL-106, CL-107).
- [ ] Gated rows sourced only from client-provided access or evidence (CL-109).
- [ ] Every evidence gap and gap-filling decision logged in the row notes (CL-112).

<!-- generated from skills/cloning-replication/site-discovery/SKILL.md -->

# site-discovery

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D16 Cloning & Replication (CL)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://github.com/internetarchive/wayback/blob/master/wayback-cdx-server/README.md ; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309.html
- **Depends on:** clone-ethics
- **Feeds into:** page-inventory

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an authorized replication or migration engagement begins and the target's full URL space — routes, templates, and states — must be established before anything is inventoried or built. This skill produces the reconciled discovery record (live crawl, sitemap, archive lists) that page-inventory consumes.
- **Do NOT use when:** no D14 clone-ethics authorization record exists yet (run clone-ethics first; this skill refuses to start), the task is the inventory table itself (page-inventory), asset capture (asset-harvesting), or general evidence harvesting for the detection pipeline (X-Crawl owns that; DET-CRWL parameters gate it).

## Rules

1. **CL-001 — Authorization artifact precedes the first request.** No target request of any kind — no discovery crawl, no sitemap fetch, no archive enumeration — runs before the project's clone-ethics authorization record exists, is dated, names the target domains in scope, and predates the first crawl log entry. The robots.txt and sitemap fetches under CL-003 are the first authorized step, taken only after the record exists. The crawl tooling checks for the record and fails closed when it is absent, stale, or out of scope. A verbal go-ahead or a record written after crawling started does not satisfy this rule.
2. **CL-002 — The crawler identifies itself honestly.** Every request carries a user agent naming the project and a contact address. The crawler never spoofs a consumer browser user agent, rotates identities to evade throttling, or otherwise disguises automated access as human browsing.
3. **CL-003 — Robots and sitemap are fetched first, and the check is logged.** For each in-scope domain, fetch `robots.txt` and the sitemap index before the first content request, and log the robots check with its date in the crawl log. A domain with no robots.txt is logged as "no robots.txt" — absence is recorded, never silently assumed.
4. **CL-004 — Disallow and crawl-delay are honored in full.** A path matched by a Disallow rule is recorded as "excluded by robots" and never fetched; a stated crawl-delay sets the minimum request interval. Per RFC 9309, robots rules "are not a form of access authorization": a missing Disallow is crawl access only and grants no reuse rights in anything discovered.
5. **CL-005 — Request rate stays inside the recorded limit.** The crawl plan states a maximum request rate per host before the run; the crawler enforces it, backs off on 429/503 responses, and the crawl log shows the observed rate. Discovery that degrades the target's availability is a failed run, however complete its output.
6. **CL-006 — The URL space comes from at least three independent sources.** Build three lists: (a) a browser-rendered crawl from the home page, (b) the XML sitemap(s), (c) the Wayback CDX index queried with `matchType=domain` (or `prefix` per host). When the client provides analytics or Search Console top pages, add them as a fourth source. A single-source list is a draft, never a discovery result.
7. **CL-007 — Every cross-source difference is reconciled in writing.** Diff the lists; each URL present in one source and absent from another gets a reconciliation note (redirected, archived-only, robots-excluded, JS-routed, gated, removed). No URL is dropped silently, and discovery is not complete while any difference is unexplained.
8. **CL-008 — JavaScript routes are discovered, not assumed away.** The crawl runs in a real browser engine so JS-rendered links resolve, and route manifests are extracted from the served JS bundles to expose client-side routes no anchor points to. Routes found only in bundles enter the crawl list tagged `js-route` and are spot-checked against the rendered site.
9. **CL-009 — Gated space is recorded as gated, never entered by bypass.** Discovery never authenticates with borrowed, shared, or client-unrelated credentials, never routes around a login or paywall, and never fetches a URL the authorization does not cover. Login-walled and paywalled URL spaces are recorded as gated with the evidence that shows they exist (sitemap entry, CDX capture, bundle route).
10. **CL-010 — Discovery records structure, not content rights.** The deliverable is URLs, statuses, template hints, and provenance — never copied page text, images, or marks. Nothing discovered here licenses reusing the target's copy, imagery, or branding; rights decisions belong to clone-ethics and asset-harvesting.
11. **CL-011 — Every discovered URL carries provenance.** Each URL in the discovery record is tagged with the source list(s) that found it (`crawl`, `sitemap`, `cdx`, `analytics`), its HTTP status or archive status, and the discovery date. A URL with no provenance tag is treated as unverified and cannot pass to page-inventory.
12. **CL-012 — Thin evidence triggers the fallback, and archive exclusion routes to D14.** When CDX coverage or a sitemap is missing or sparse, fall back to client-provided exports and analytics lists and record which sources were unavailable; the three-source gate (G-CL-003) then runs on the sources that exist, with the gap stated. If the target's robots.txt excludes archiving or crawling outright, stop and route the case to clone-ethics (D14) — the exclusion may signal against capture generally, and discovery does not decide that question itself.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CL-001 — Crawl first, authorize later.** Banned: any discovery crawl that starts before the clone-ethics authorization record exists and predates it. Defeats: DET-CRWL-014. Bad: the agent crawls a client's old site "just to scope it" on Monday; the authorization record is filed Friday. Instead: commit the authorization record first and let the pre-flight gate (G-CL-001) refuse any earlier crawl, under CL-001. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-002 — Fetching robots-disallowed paths.** Banned: requesting any URL matched by the target's robots.txt Disallow rules, for any reason, including "just to confirm it exists". Defeats: DET-CRWL-014. Bad: the crawl log shows 14 fetches under `/internal/` because the crawler's robots handling was switched off to "get the full picture". Instead: record each disallowed space as "excluded by robots" without fetching it, under CL-004. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-003 — Completing discovery through a login or paywall bypass.** Banned: enumerating gated URL space using borrowed or shared credentials, a harvested session cookie, or a mirror/cache route around a login wall or paywall. Defeats: DET-CRWL-008. Bad: a teammate's personal account login is used to crawl the members' area so the route list looks complete. Instead: record the space as gated with its public evidence and proceed only through access the client legitimately provides, under CL-009. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-004 — Home-page links declared "fully mapped".** Banned: presenting a crawl of home-page links alone as the site's complete URL space, with orphan, archived-only, and JS-routed pages silently absent. Defeats: DET-CRWL-013. Bad: the discovery report claims "site fully mapped: 38 pages" from one crawl, while the sitemap lists 112 URLs and the CDX index holds 40 more, none of them checked. Instead: build the three source lists and reconcile every difference in writing before claiming completeness, under CL-006 and CL-007. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CL-005 — The disguised crawler.** Banned: sending a spoofed consumer-browser user agent, rotating user agents or IPs to evade rate limits, or stripping identifying headers so automated discovery reads as human traffic. Defeats: DET-CRWL-016. Bad: the crawler presents as "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0) Chrome" with no project identity after the target begins throttling it. Instead: identify the project and a contact in the user agent and slow down or stop when throttled, under CL-002 and CL-005. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CL-001 — Authorization pre-flight check.** Verifies: CL-001. Check (automated): before the crawler starts, a script asserts the project's clone-ethics authorization record file exists, is dated, names the target domains, covers discovery of those domains, and its commit timestamp predates the current run. Pass: record complete, in scope, and pre-committed. Fail: the crawler refuses to start (fail closed); no partial crawl is permitted. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — the authorization record names the pattern class and zero target domains, and its timestamp is compared against the first inventory artifact; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-002 — Robots and terms compliance check.** Verifies: CL-003, CL-004, CL-005. Check (automated): the crawl log is grepped against each domain's robots.txt Disallow set — any fetched disallowed path fails; the log must also show a robots fetch per domain before its first content request, the identifying user agent on every request, and an observed request rate at or under the crawl plan's limit. Pass: zero disallowed fetches, robots logged first, identity and rate compliant. Fail: block delivery of the discovery record; each breach is filed as a finding. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — no domain is fetched, so compliance is evidenced by the zero-fetch crawl log and the record's no-target scope; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-003 — Three-source reconciliation check.** Verifies: CL-006, CL-007, CL-012. Check (automated + manual): a script diffs the crawl, sitemap, and CDX URL lists and lists every URL not present in all sources; each listed URL must carry a reconciliation note in the discovery record. Where a source was unavailable, the record states the gap and the fallback used. Pass: zero unexplained differences. Fail: block; discovery is incomplete until every difference is explained or the URL is carried into page-inventory with its note. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — the pattern inventory replaces the crawl, sitemap, and CDX lists as the reconciliation source; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-004 — JS-route spot-check.** Verifies: CL-008. Check (manual): pick 5 routes found only in JS bundle manifests; load each in a browser and confirm the route renders and matches its discovery-record entry (URL, status, template hint). Pass: all 5 confirmed. Fail: re-extract route manifests and re-run the rendered crawl before discovery closes. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: NOT APPLICABLE — no JS bundle manifests exist and no target page may be loaded; route existence rests on the pattern inventory; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.
- **G-CL-005 — Gated-space and provenance audit.** Verifies: CL-009, CL-010, CL-011. Check (automated + manual): assert every URL in the discovery record carries at least one provenance tag and a status; assert no fetched URL required authentication (no session cookies or Authorization headers in the crawl log); assert every gated space appears as a gated record, not as fetched pages. Pass: provenance complete, zero authenticated fetches, gated spaces recorded as gated. Fail: block; the offending fetches are removed from the record and filed as findings. Recorded in: progress.md. Pattern-reference mode: ADAPTED — provenance tags read “pattern reference” and the zero-authenticated-fetch assertion is evidenced by the zero-fetch crawl log; see the pattern-reference disposition table in the clone-rebuild playbook.

## Anti-patterns

- **The sitemap treated as the site.** The sitemap is one source of three; it routinely omits new, orphaned, and utility pages. Catch it by never closing discovery until the crawl and CDX lists have been diffed against it (G-CL-003).
- **Reconciliation by deletion.** Cross-source differences are "resolved" by deleting the odd URL from the list instead of explaining it. Catch it by counting: the reconciled record's URL total must be at least the largest single source's total, with notes accounting for the rest.
- **Completeness theater.** The report says "full URL space" while the crawl depth, rate limit, or robots exclusions quietly truncated coverage. Catch it by stating crawl depth, exclusions, and unavailable sources in the record itself — coverage claims must name their limits.
- **Discovery drifting into harvesting.** Page bodies, images, and copy start accumulating in the discovery folder "for reference". Catch it by checking the discovery output contains URLs and metadata only; content capture belongs to asset-harvesting under its own rights decisions.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — Discovery launched on a verbal OK](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects CL-001.
- [Example 2 — "Fully mapped" from the home page](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects CL-006, CL-007.
- [Example 3 — The members' area, enumerated with a borrowed login](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects CL-009.

## Recall anchors

- No authorization record, no first request — the crawler fails closed.
- Three lists or it is a draft: crawl, sitemap, CDX — every difference explained.
- Disallowed means recorded, never fetched.
- Gated means recorded as gated, never entered.
- Discovery maps structure; it grants no rights in anything it finds.

## Checklist

- [ ] The clone-ethics authorization record is committed, dated, and covers the target domains — and predates the first crawl log entry (CL-001, G-CL-001).
- [ ] robots.txt and the sitemap index were fetched and logged per domain before any content request (CL-003, G-CL-002).
- [ ] No disallowed path was fetched; each is recorded as "excluded by robots" (CL-004, G-CL-002).
- [ ] The crawler identified the project and contact, and stayed inside the recorded rate limit (CL-002, CL-005, G-CL-002).
- [ ] Crawl, sitemap, and CDX lists are built and every difference carries a reconciliation note (CL-006, CL-007, G-CL-003).
- [ ] JS-bundle routes are extracted, tagged, and spot-checked in a browser (CL-008, G-CL-004).
- [ ] No login, paywall, or access control was bypassed; gated spaces are recorded as gated (CL-009, G-CL-005).
- [ ] Every URL carries provenance tags and a status, and the record holds URLs and metadata only — no copied content (CL-010, CL-011, G-CL-005).

## Department D17 — ai-features

# ai-cost-control

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/red-team/owasp-llm-top-10/ ; https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/cost-tracking
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, ai-observability
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an AI feature is being designed, routed to a model, given quotas or budgets, or reviewed for spend — and whenever a cost or savings figure about an AI feature is about to be stated anywhere.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is recording traces and usage in the first place (use ai-observability; this skill consumes its metering stream), choosing a model on quality grounds alone (use ai-evaluation for the scores that justify a tier), or setting product prices (an operator business decision this skill only supplies unit costs for).

## Rules

1. **AI-181 — Every feature has a named budget and an owner.** Before release, each AI feature records in configuration: a per-request token budget, a per-user quota, a per-period spend budget, and the person or role who owns them. A feature with no recorded budget does not ship; "the provider invoice" is never the first signal of overspend.
2. **AI-182 — Cost is computed from metered usage, never hard-coded rates.** The wrapper records tokens in and out for every call (see ai-observability), and cost is computed as metered tokens multiplied by the operator's current price sheet. The price sheet lives in one configuration location, names its source and the date it was last checked, and is the only thing that changes when a provider reprices; no price, rate, or per-call cost figure is written into feature code.
3. **AI-183 — Caps are enforced in the wrapper, server-side.** When a per-user quota or a per-feature budget is reached, the wrapper stops the call or degrades it (AI-188) before any provider request is made. An alert, email, or dashboard warning by itself is not enforcement and does not satisfy this rule.
4. **AI-184 — Retries and loops have hard bounds.** Every call path records a maximum retry count with backoff, a maximum iteration count for agent or tool loops, and a maximum spend per task or session. Hitting any bound terminates the path with a typed error; there is no code path in which a failure can retry, loop, or re-plan without limit.
5. **AI-185 — Model tier is justified by eval scores at that tier.** Simple tasks (classification, extraction, short rewrites) route to the smallest model whose recorded eval results meet the feature's quality floor (see ai-evaluation). Defaulting a task class to the largest available model requires a stored eval comparison showing the cheaper tier fails the floor.
6. **AI-186 — Caching is exact-match and disclosed.** Responses may be cached only for identical requests, with a cache key that includes the prompt version and model ID. A cache hit is marked as a hit in the trace and in any usage report; a cached or template response is never presented to a user or a report as a fresh model generation.
7. **AI-187 — Context is budgeted, not stuffed.** Prompt assembly enforces a maximum input-token budget per request. Retrieved chunks, history, and examples are selected or truncated by a stated policy that fits the budget; assembly never sends whatever happens to fit the provider's context window.
8. **AI-188 — Degradation is graceful and honest.** When a budget or quota is exhausted, the feature degrades along a documented path — cheaper model, reduced context, non-AI fallback, or a plain statement that the feature is unavailable — and the trace records that degradation occurred. Silently lowering quality while presenting the output as full-strength is forbidden.
9. **AI-189 — Every paid-model endpoint has a per-user quota.** Quotas and rate limits apply to authenticated and unauthenticated endpoints alike, are enforced server-side, and are counted from server-side records. A limit that lives only in client state, a cookie, or the UI does not count as a quota.
10. **AI-190 — Cost is reported per feature and per model.** On a fixed cycle, each feature's report shows metered usage, spend against its budget, and unit cost (spend divided by successful tasks or requests), broken down by model. A feature whose unit cost crosses its recorded threshold is flagged for a routing, caching, or retirement review — an unprofitable feature must be visible, not averaged away.
11. **AI-191 — Abuse is treated as a cost attack.** Maximal-size requests, high-frequency calls from one identity, and inputs designed to induce loops or maximal output are rate-limited and bounded like any other unbounded-consumption threat (OWASP LLM10:2025). Cost limits are part of the security design, not only the finance design.
12. **AI-192 — A cost figure carries its provenance.** Any cost, unit-cost, or savings figure stated in a UI, report, or release note names the metering period, the feature scope, and the price-sheet date it was computed from. A figure that cannot be recomputed from stored traces under AI-182 is not published.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-091 — Alert-only cap presented as enforcement.** Banned: a budget or quota whose only effect at the limit is sending an alert, while calls continue and the UI shows the feature as "protected." Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Bad: the admin panel shows "Monthly cap set — spend protected," the cap passes on a Tuesday, an email goes to an unmonitored inbox, and calls run unbounded until the invoice arrives. Instead: enforce the cap in the wrapper before the provider call (AI-183) and degrade honestly at the limit (AI-188); alerts are an addition to enforcement, never a substitute. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-092 — Frozen cost dashboard.** Banned: an AI spend or usage display rendered from constants, estimates typed into config, or a one-time snapshot, presented as the feature's actual consumption. Defeats: DET-FAKE-004. Bad: the "AI costs" panel shows a tidy figure computed at launch from expected volume; real usage triples and the panel never moves. Instead: compute every displayed figure from the metered traces for the stated period (AI-182, AI-190). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-093 — Silent canned or cached substitution.** Banned: serving stored, template, or previously generated responses in place of model calls to save money, while the UI and reports present them as live model output. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Bad: similar prompts are answered from a template table "to control costs," users believe they are talking to the model, and usage reports count the answers as generations. Instead: cache only identical requests, mark hits in the trace, and disclose any non-model fallback where it is served (AI-186, AI-188). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-094 — Cost report fabricated from hard-coded rates.** Banned: a cost report or export whose figures are computed from prices or per-call costs written into code or a spreadsheet, rather than from metered tokens and the current price sheet. Defeats: DET-FAKE-019. Bad: the monthly export multiplies request counts by a per-call price typed in at launch; the provider repriced twice since, and finance is reconciling against numbers that were never real. Instead: generate every report from stored traces with the dated price sheet named on it (AI-182, AI-192). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-095 — Client-side quota counter.** Banned: a per-user AI usage limit counted in browser state, local storage, or a cookie, so reloading, clearing storage, or calling the API directly resets it. Defeats: DET-FAKE-005. Bad: free-tier users get "10 AI summaries a day" enforced by a counter in the page; a hard reload restores all 10 and a script bypasses the limit entirely. Instead: count usage in server-side records keyed to the user or identity and enforce the quota in the wrapper (AI-189, AI-183). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-091 — Budget-guard test.** Verifies: AI-181, AI-183, AI-189. Check (automated): in staging, set a low test per-user quota and a low test per-feature budget, then drive scripted traffic past both. Pass: once each limit is reached, further provider calls are stopped or degraded per AI-188, the alert fires, and the trace records the enforcement; zero provider calls occur past the cap. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-092 — Runaway-loop test.** Verifies: AI-184, AI-191. Check (automated): fault-inject with a provider stub that returns retryable errors indefinitely, plus a tool-loop scenario whose plan never converges. Pass: both paths terminate at the recorded retry, iteration, or spend bound with a typed error, and total tokens consumed stay at or below the bound's ceiling. Fail: block release — an uncapped loop is a release blocker. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-093 — Metering reconciliation.** Verifies: AI-182, AI-190. Check (automated): run a known set of test calls with recorded token counts, then recompute the feature's reported spend from the stored traces and the current price sheet. Pass: every test call has a trace with tokens in/out and model ID, and the recomputed total matches the reported total exactly. Fail: cost reporting is treated as unmeasured and fixed before the next report is published. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-094 — Routing evidence check.** Verifies: AI-185. Check (manual): open the routing configuration for each feature and list every task class with its assigned model tier. Pass: each tier assignment links an eval report at that tier meeting the feature's floor, and any largest-tier assignment links the comparison showing the cheaper tier fails. Fail: unproven task classes are re-routed to the smallest tier or the eval is run before release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-095 — Degradation drill.** Verifies: AI-186, AI-188. Check (manual): exhaust a test budget in staging and use the feature as an end user, including repeating an earlier request exactly. Pass: the user sees the documented fallback or a clear unavailability statement, any cached answer is identifiable as cached in the trace, and nothing is presented as full-strength model output that was not generated at full strength. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Invoice-driven discovery.** Nobody can say what a feature costs until the provider bill lands, and the post-mortem is an argument about whose usage it was. Catch it by asking for last cycle's per-feature report (AI-190): if it does not exist, cost control does not exist either.
- **Blended-average comfort.** A single average cost per request across all features hides the one feature burning the budget behind nine cheap ones. Catch it by refusing any cost report without the per-feature, per-model breakdown AI-190 requires.
- **Retry-as-reliability.** Flaky outputs are "fixed" by raising retry counts and timeouts, quietly multiplying spend per successful task. Catch it in review: any retry-count increase without a bound check against AI-184 and a unit-cost note is a cost change disguised as a reliability change.
- **Launch-day price sheet.** The price sheet was copied once at launch and never re-checked, so every computed cost has been drifting from reality since the first repricing. Catch it by reading the sheet's recorded check date (AI-182): an old date invalidates every figure derived from it.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — The cap that only sent an email](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects AI-183 (BAN-AI-091).
- [Example 2 — The retry loop that billed all weekend](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects AI-184.
- [Example 3 — The dashboard that never moved](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects AI-182, AI-190 (BAN-AI-092).

## Recall anchors

- No recorded budget and owner, no ship — the invoice is never the first signal.
- Cost = metered tokens × the operator's current price sheet; rates never live in code.
- A cap that only alerts does not exist; enforcement happens in the wrapper, before the call.
- Every retry, loop, and task has a hard bound — an uncapped loop is a release blocker.
- Cheapest tier the evals justify, honest degradation at the limit, per-feature reports or it didn't happen.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every AI feature has a recorded per-request token budget, per-user quota, per-period budget, and a named owner (AI-181).
- [ ] The wrapper meters tokens in/out per call, and cost is computed from the dated price sheet in its single config location — no rates in feature code (AI-182, G-AI-093).
- [ ] The budget-guard test passes: past the cap, calls stop or degrade and zero provider calls leak through (AI-183, AI-189, G-AI-091).
- [ ] Retry counts, loop iterations, and per-task spend all have recorded hard bounds, and the runaway-loop test terminates at them (AI-184, G-AI-092).
- [ ] Every task class routes to a tier backed by an eval report at that tier; largest-tier assignments carry their justification (AI-185, G-AI-094).
- [ ] Caching is exact-match, keyed on prompt version and model, with hits marked in traces and reports; prompt assembly enforces the input-token budget with a stated truncation policy (AI-186, AI-187).
- [ ] The degradation drill passes: at the limit the user gets the documented fallback or a clear unavailability statement, recorded in the trace (AI-188, G-AI-095).
- [ ] The latest per-feature, per-model cost report exists, and every published cost figure names its period, scope, and price-sheet date (AI-190, AI-192).

# ai-evaluation

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-getting-started ; https://www.n4n.ai/blog/golden-datasets-for-llm-evals-how-to-build-one
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, prompt-engineering
- **Feeds into:** prompt-engineering, rag-retrieval, search-relevance, recommendations, ai-observability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an AI feature is being built or changed — new prompt, model, retrieval, or configuration — and its quality must be measured before release, or when a quality figure about an AI feature is about to be stated anywhere.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is screening inputs/outputs for safety (use ai-safety), tuning search ranking against a judgment set (use search-relevance, which applies this skill's discipline to NDCG), or watching live traffic (use ai-observability). This skill owns the offline golden-set measurement that gates changes.

## Rules

1. **AI-141 — No golden dataset, no ship.** Every AI feature owns a golden dataset — fixed inputs, each with a reference answer or an explicit grading rubric and a category — stored as a single versioned artifact in the repo. A feature without one does not release, and an eval run once at launch and never again counts as no eval.
2. **AI-142 — Items come from real usage.** Dataset items are seeded from production logs, support failures, and observed failure modes, not invented happy paths. Each item records its source (log, ticket, incident, or authored edge case) so its realism is auditable.
3. **AI-143 — Failure and adversarial categories are mandatory.** The dataset includes, as named categories: malformed and empty inputs, unanswerable questions where abstention is the correct behavior, refusal cases, and adversarial inputs (injection attempts, contradictory instructions). A dataset of only well-formed, answerable questions is incomplete by definition.
4. **AI-144 — Graders run cheapest-first.** Grading stacks deterministic checks first (exact match, schema validity, forbidden strings, required citations), then similarity measures, then a model judge only for criteria no cheaper grader can decide. Every item names which grader decides it.
5. **AI-145 — The judge is pinned and calibrated.** A model judge's model ID and temperature are pinned in the eval config. Before its scores may gate anything, its agreement with human labels is measured on a labeled calibration sample and recorded; it is re-measured at every judge model or judge-prompt change. Below the recorded agreement floor, judge scores are advisory only.
6. **AI-146 — The dataset is reviewed like code.** Dataset changes land as reviewed, versioned diffs with a stated reason. Correcting a wrong reference answer or an ambiguous rubric is legitimate; changing an item because the current stack fails it is not, and the diff must say which of the two it is.
7. **AI-147 — Eval data and tuning data are disjoint.** No golden item, and no near-duplicate of one, appears in prompts, few-shot examples, or fine-tuning data. The eval measures generalization, never memorization of the test itself.
8. **AI-148 — Every change runs the eval.** Any change to a prompt, model ID, retrieval configuration, or grading-relevant parameter triggers a full eval run in CI before merge or release. There is no "trivial change" exemption; wording changes are exactly what evals exist to catch.
9. **AI-149 — Floors and tolerances are set in advance.** Each feature's eval config records, before any run: the minimum overall pass rate for release and the maximum allowed regression per category. A threshold may not be lowered in the same change whose run fails it.
10. **AI-150 — Results are recorded per version.** Every run stores a report naming the prompt version, model ID, retrieval config, and dataset version, with the overall pass rate, the per-category breakdown, and the list of failed items — not just an aggregate number. Reports are kept with the change that produced them.
11. **AI-151 — Production failures feed the dataset.** Failed production cases surfaced by ai-observability (user corrections, escalations, thumbs-down traces) are triaged on a fixed cycle: each is added to the golden dataset as a new item, or rejected with a recorded reason. The dataset version bumps when items are added.
12. **AI-152 — A quality figure carries its provenance.** Any pass rate or quality claim stated in a UI, report, or release note names the dataset version, the stack version, and the run date. A figure that cannot be traced to a stored report (AI-150) is not published.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-071 — Fixture eval scored as production quality.** Banned: running the eval against a stubbed model, fixture responses, or a demo pipeline, then reporting the score as the real feature's quality. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Bad: the eval harness points at recorded model replies so CI stays green in seconds, and the release notes cite its 100% pass rate. Instead: the runner executes the real wrapper, prompt, model, and retrieval stack end to end (AI-148); stubs belong only in llm-integration's fault-injection tests. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-072 — The test edited to pass.** Banned: deleting, rewording, or re-rubric-ing golden items after a run fails them, so the next run passes without the stack improving. Defeats: DET-FAKE-004. Bad: three failing refund questions are quietly removed from the dataset the night before release, and the dashboard shows the pass rate climbing. Instead: item changes go through reviewed diffs with a correctness reason (AI-146); a genuinely wrong reference is fixed openly and the fix is visible in the version history. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-073 — Happy-path showcase set presented as the eval.** Banned: a small set of easy, well-formed demo questions standing in for the golden dataset, with its score reported as measured quality. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Bad: twenty polished questions the demo always nails are labeled "evaluation: 95% accurate," while malformed inputs, unanswerable questions, and injection attempts are never tested. Instead: build the dataset from real usage with the mandatory failure and adversarial categories (AI-142, AI-143). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-074 — Uncalibrated judge presented as measurement.** Banned: a model judge's scores displayed or gated on as precise quality metrics with no human-labeled calibration behind them. Defeats: DET-FAKE-018. Bad: a dashboard shows "Answer quality: 94.2%" from a judge that has never been compared against a single human label, and releases are approved on its movement. Instead: pin the judge, measure its agreement with human labels on a calibration sample, and publish scores only with that agreement recorded (AI-145, AI-152). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-075 — Grading the memorized test.** Banned: tuning prompts, few-shot examples, or fine-tuning data on golden items or near-duplicates, then citing the same set's score as held-out performance. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Bad: the twelve hardest eval questions are pasted into the prompt as worked examples; the eval passes 100% and the first unseen user question fails. Instead: keep eval and tuning data disjoint and scan for overlap before a run counts (AI-147, G-AI-073). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-071 — CI eval gate.** Verifies: AI-141, AI-148, AI-149, AI-150. Check (automated): on any change to prompt files, model configuration, or retrieval configuration, CI runs the feature's eval runner against the committed dataset (e.g. `python evals/run_evals.py --feature <feature> --dataset evals/<feature>/golden.jsonl --config evals/<feature>/config.yaml`, adjusted to the project's runner) and writes the report into the change record. Pass: overall pass rate at or above the floor recorded in the eval config, and no category regresses beyond its recorded tolerance. Fail: block merge and release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-072 — Judge calibration check.** Verifies: AI-145. Check (automated): run the pinned judge over the feature's human-labeled calibration sample and compute its agreement with the human labels; store the result with the judge model ID and temperature. Pass: agreement at or above the floor recorded in the eval config. Fail: judge scores are advisory only and may not gate a release until re-calibration passes. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-073 — Dataset integrity and contamination scan.** Verifies: AI-141, AI-143, AI-147. Check (automated): a script over the dataset file asserts every item has a category, a source, and a reference answer or rubric; asserts the mandatory failure and adversarial categories are non-empty; and asserts no item's normalized text matches or near-duplicates any prompt few-shot example or tuning file in the repo. Pass: zero violations. Fail: block the eval run from counting toward G-AI-071. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-074 — Change-record eval audit.** Verifies: AI-148, AI-150, AI-152. Check (manual): pick the most recent prompt, model, or retrieval change for the feature and open its change record. Pass: the record links a stored eval report naming prompt version, model ID, dataset version, overall and per-category results, and the delta against the previous version. Fail: the change is treated as unmeasured and re-run before the next release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-075 — Production-failure intake review.** Verifies: AI-151. Check (manual): at the feature's review cycle, list the failed production cases flagged by ai-observability since the last review. Pass: every case is either present as a new golden item (dataset version bumped) or carries a recorded rejection reason. Fail: intake is completed before the next release is approved. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Anti-patterns

- **Vibes-based comparison.** Two versions are compared by eyeballing a handful of outputs and declaring the new one "better." Catch it by asking for the run report: if no dataset version and pass rates exist, the comparison never happened, however convincing the samples look.
- **Aggregate-only reporting.** A single overall pass rate is quoted while one category — usually abstention or adversarial — has silently collapsed to zero. Catch it by refusing any report without the per-category breakdown AI-150 requires.
- **Stale golden set.** The dataset has not changed in months while the product, corpus, and user behavior moved on; the eval now certifies last year's feature. Catch it by checking the dataset's version history against the production-failure intake (G-AI-075): no new items means intake is not happening.
- **Rubric-free judge prompts.** The judge is told to "score quality from 1–10" with no rubric, examples, or pinned settings, so its scores drift with phrasing and cannot be compared across runs. Catch it by reading the judge prompt in the eval config: no rubric and no pinned model means the numbers are decoration.

## Examples

- [Example 1 — The 95% showcase set](examples/example-1.md) — violates/corrects AI-142, AI-143 (BAN-AI-073).
- [Example 2 — The failing questions that disappeared](examples/example-2.md) — violates/corrects AI-146 (BAN-AI-072).
- [Example 3 — The judge nobody calibrated](examples/example-3.md) — violates/corrects AI-145 (BAN-AI-074).

## Recall anchors

- No golden dataset, no ship — and launch-day-only counts as none.
- Items come from real failures, not invented happy paths.
- Cheapest grader first; the judge is pinned and calibrated.
- Never edit the test to pass; never tune on the test.
- "It felt better" is not a release criterion — the recorded delta is.

## Checklist

- [ ] The feature has a versioned golden dataset in the repo, seeded from real usage, with source recorded per item (AI-141, AI-142).
- [ ] Failure, adversarial, refusal, and unanswerable/abstention categories exist and are non-empty (AI-143, G-AI-073).
- [ ] Each item names its grader, stacked cheapest-first: deterministic, similarity, then judge (AI-144).
- [ ] The judge model and temperature are pinned, and its agreement with human labels is measured and recorded (AI-145, G-AI-072).
- [ ] Dataset changes are reviewed, versioned diffs with correctness reasons — none made to rescue a failing run (AI-146).
- [ ] No golden item or near-duplicate appears in prompts, few-shot examples, or tuning data; contamination scan is clean (AI-147, G-AI-073).
- [ ] The eval ran in CI for this change; overall pass rate meets the pre-recorded floor and no category regressed beyond tolerance (AI-148, AI-149, G-AI-071).
- [ ] The report is stored with prompt/model/dataset versions, per-category results, and failed items, and any published figure cites that provenance (AI-150, AI-152).
